title: Minimality conjecture for initial threshold graphs generated by RFI
record_statement: Let $N>0$ and $r\geq 2$ be fixed, and let $I=(0,N]$. Let $T_G(a_1,\ldots,a_r)$ be the initial threshold graph obtained from RFI$(N,r)$. **Minimality conjecture.** The graph $G$ is minimal: if $\widetilde{G}\preceq G$ is also $I$-eigenvalue free, then $\widetilde{G}=G$. This conjecture asserts that no smaller threshold graph is $(0,N]$-eigenvalue free. The authors report exhaustive computational searches for several positive values of $N$ that found no smaller example, but the general claim remains open.
source: Luiz Emilio Allem, Elismar R. Oliveira and Fernando Tura, “On I-eigenvalue free threshold graphs”, arXiv:2110.12107 (2021).
row_statement: For every real N > 0 and every depth r >= 2, the threshold graph that the source's algorithm produces with the smallest choice at every step is minimal: any threshold graph of the same depth whose block sizes are coordinatewise at most those of the initial graph and which has no adjacency eigenvalue in (0, N] is the initial graph itself. The source's authors conjectured this after exhaustive searches of millions of graphs. The proof reduces freeness of the interval to positive definiteness of a k x k matrix (k = ceil(r/2)) by the block structure and a Schur complement on the independent blocks, and shows that every single decrement of a block fails: for a clique block the pivot at the greedy threshold becomes nonpositive, and for an independent block a floor inequality makes the pivot of the pair formed with the preceding clique block nonpositive. Lean defines the graph on a sigma type, the algorithm with real floors, and the eigenvalue condition through adjacency eigenvectors, and includes a non-vacuity lemma.

title: The asymptotic threshold conjecture for complete bipartite graphs
record_statement:
Let $K_{2,l}$ be the complete bipartite graph with parts of sizes $2$ and $l$, and let $\tau(K_{2,l})$ denote its list color function threshold.

**Asymptotic threshold conjecture.**

$$
\tau(K_{2,l}) = \Theta(\sqrt{l}) \quad\text{as } l \rightarrow \infty.
$$

The preceding theorem proves a lower bound of order $\sqrt{l}$, while the conjecture asserts a matching upper bound and hence determines the asymptotic growth rate of the threshold.

Let $T$ be a complete full $t$-ary tree, meaning a rooted tree in which every nonleaf has exactly $t$ children and all leaves have the same depth. Let $l$ be the number of leaves and let $\chi_{la}(T)$ be the local antimagic chromatic number. **Even-arity complete full tree conjecture.** For every even integer $t\geq2$,

title: Thue–Morse arithmetic-progression bound conjecture
record_statement:
Let $\mathbf{t}$ denote the Thue–Morse sequence, and let $A_{\mathbf{t}}(d)$ be its associated arithmetic-progression counting function.

**Thue–Morse bound conjecture.** For all $d \geq 1$,

$$
A_{\mathbf{t}}(d) \leq d+5.
$$

Moreover, equality holds if and only if $d=2^k-1$ for some even $k \geq 2$.
The conjecture gives a sharp linear upper bound, with equality at the indicated powers-of-two-minus-one parameters.
source: Bartosz Sobolewski, “On monochromatic arithmetic progressions in binary words associated with pattern sequences”, arXiv:2204.05287 (2023).
row_statement: For every difference d >= 1, the longest monochromatic arithmetic progression of difference d in the Thue-Morse sequence has length A_t(d) <= d + 5, and A_t(d) = d + 5 exactly when d = 2^k - 1 with k even and k >= 2 (d = 3, 15, 63, 255, ...). This is Conjecture 3 of Sobolewski, for every starting point and both colours. The proof places a binomial cube S_D with D >= c - 5 inside the set of residues where the colour is forced to change, by Lucas's theorem; shows over F_2 that X^{uj}(1 + X^u)^D is divisible by (1 + X)^D, so that after multiplication by any odd u this set cannot fit in a cyclic arc shorter than D, which gives the bound; and characterizes equality by a rigidity lemma for affine cubes and three explicit families of obstructions. Lean defines the length with no cap, as the supremum over starting points of the first index at which the colour changes, in the extended naturals.

title: Injectivity conjecture for evaluation maps of linearized polynomials
record_statement:
Let $L=L(x)$ be a $q$-polynomial in $F[x]$ of $q$-degree $n$, where $F$ is a field of characteristic $p$ that contains $\operatorname{\mathbb{F}}_q$. Assume that $L$ is not a $q^s$-polynomial for $s>1$, and that $L(x)/x$ is irreducible over $F$.

**Injectivity conjecture.** If $1\le r\le q-1$, then the evaluation map $\epsilon_r$ is injective.

This conjecture predicts injectivity in the range $1\le r\le q-1$ under irreducibility and a non-$q^s$-polynomial hypothesis. The surrounding results establish related injectivity statements for evaluation maps, but the supplied text does not state whether this conjecture has been resolved.
source: Rod Gow and Gary McGuire, “Linearized Polynomials, Galois Groups and Symmetric Power Modules”, arXiv:2206.01551 (2022).
row_statement: Conjecture 1 of Gow and McGuire is false. The roots are the image of u F_81, with u^80 = t, under the additive twist x -> x + x^3 of the Kummer polynomial X^81 - tX; the twist keeps irreducibility, because the automorphisms u -> cu act transitively on the nonzero roots, and it forces the kernel. title: Congruence-class bias conjecture for parts in k-regular partitions
record_statement:
For $k$-regular partitions, let $D_k(r,t;n)$ denote the number of occurrences of parts congruent to $r$ modulo $t$ among the partitions of $n$. Here $t\geq 6$, $1\leq r<s\leq t$, and $k\geq 3$.

**Congruence-class bias conjecture.** For $n\geq 1$,

$$
D_k(r,t;n) \geq D_k(s,t;n).
$$

Moreover, for $k\geq 2$, if

$$
n>\max\{t+3,16\},
$$

then

$$
D_k(r,t;n)>D_k(s,t;n).
$$

The conjecture formalizes the observed bias toward smaller parts and extends the finite computational verification to all $t\geq 6$ and all admissible congruence classes. The preceding theorem establishes related bounds for $2\leq k,t\leq 10$, while the asserted ranges beyond those finite checks remain open.
source: Faye Jackson and Misheel Otgonbayar, “Biases among Congruence Classes for Parts in k-regular Partitions”, arXiv:2207.04352 (2022).
row_statement: Let D_k(r,t;n) count all occurrences, with multiplicity, of parts congruent to r modulo t among partitions of n in which each part occurs fewer than k times. For all t≥6 and 1≤r<s≤t, D_k(r,t;n)≥D_k(s,t;n) for k≥3 and n≥1, and D_k(r,t;n)>D_k(s,t;n) for k≥2 and n>max(t+3,16).

title: Growth conjecture for the number of orderings of congruence-class biases
record_statement:
Let $\mathscr{O}(t)$ denote the number of possible orderings arising from the biases among congruence classes for $k$-indivisible partitions, and let $\varphi(t)$ be Euler's totient function. **Growth conjecture.** As $t\to\infty$, we have

$$
\frac{\mathscr{O}(t)}{\varphi(t)}=o(t)
$$

and

$$
\log t=o\left(\frac{\mathscr{O}(t)}{\varphi(t)}\right).
$$

Thus the normalized number of orderings is conjectured to grow sublinearly in $t$ and faster than logarithmically. The claim is motivated by numerical evidence and remains open.
source: Faye Jackson and Misheel Otgonbayar, “Unexpected Biases between Congruence Classes for Parts in k-indivisible Partitions”, arXiv:2207.06365 (2022).

title: The cycle complement stable-set polynomial conjecture
record_statement:
Let $C_n$ be the cycle graph on $n$ vertices, let $p(C_n;z)$ denote its perfectly matchable set polynomial, and let $\overline{h}^*(C_n;z)$ denote the normalized $h^*$-polynomial of the stable set polytope of the complement of $C_n$. **Cycle polynomial conjecture.** For all $n\geq 4$, 

$$
\overline{h}^*(C_n; z) = p(C_n; z) + \frac{1+(-1)^{n+1}}{2}z^{(n+1)/2}.
$$

The formula agrees with the explicitly computed even-cycle case and with the listed examples through $n=9$; the asserted general identity, particularly for odd cycles, remains open in the source.
source: Robert Davis and Florian Kohl, “Perfectly Matchable Set Polynomials and h^*-polynomials for Stable Set Polytopes of Complements of Graphs”, arXiv:2207.14759 (2022).
row_statement: The conjecture holds for every n ≥ 4. The even case is Davis and Kohl's own Corollary 3.14; the new case is odd n ≥ 5, where the stable set polytope of the complement of the odd cycle is not a lattice-point-friendly compressed polytope and has the extra rank facet. The proof counts the lattice points of the dilates directly from the known facet description of the antihole (Padberg): a greedy recursion around the cycle has a unique real cyclic fixed point; expanding the integer residual weights counts matchings of the cycle, which gives the perfectly matchable set polynomial, and the half-integral fixed points give the one extra monomial z^{(n+1)/2}; a rank-2 transfer matrix assembles the generating function. Lean proves the identity for all n ≥ 4, odd and even, from the lattice-point description of the dilated polytope, so it does not depend on the source's Corollary 3.14, and checks the source's Table 2 for n = 4..7.

title: The prime-modulus conjecture for progression-free digit sets
record_statement:
Let $p\geq 13$ be a prime with $p\equiv 1\bmod 4$, and let $n$ be an integer divisible by $(p+3)/2$. For a digit set $D\subseteq\mathbb{Z}_p$, write $S(D,n)$ for the set of vectors in $\mathbb{Z}_p^n$ in which every digit of $D$ occurs the same number of times. Define

$$
D=\left\{0,1,\ldots,\frac{p-1}{2},\frac{p+3}{2}\right\}.
$$

**Prime-modulus progression-free-set conjecture.** The set $S(D,n)$ does not contain any arithmetic progression of length $4$.

This conjecture extends the progression-free constructions for odd progression lengths to a case not covered by the stated theorem, motivated by computations with small primes. Its status is unresolved in the source.
source: Christian Elsholtz, Benjamin Klahn and Gabriel F. Lipnik, “Large Subsets of Z_m^n without Arithmetic Progressions”, arXiv:2211.02588 (2022).

title: The even zigzag-poset LE-symmetry conjecture
record_statement:
For even $n$, let $Z_n$ be the poset on $n$ elements with relations

$$
v_1 < v_2 > v_3 < v_4 > \ldots > v_{n-3} < v_{n-2} > v_{n-1} < v_n.
$$

A poset is **LE-symmetric** when its Bender–Knuth group acts as the full symmetric group on its set of linear extensions. **The even zigzag-poset LE-symmetry conjecture.** The zigzag-poset $Z_n$ is LE-symmetric when $n$ is even. This is computationally verified for all even $n\leq 10$, while odd cases such as $Z_5$, $Z_7$, and $Z_9$ provide counterexamples; the even case remains open.
source: Judy Hsin-Hui Chiang, Anh Trong Nam Hoang, Matthew Kendall, Ryan Lynch, Son Nguyen, Benjamin Przybocki and Janabel Xia, “Bender-Knuth involutions on linear extensions of posets”, arXiv:2302.12425 (2024).
row_statement: For every even n the Bender–Knuth involutions generate the full symmetric group on the linear extensions of the zigzag poset Z_n (whose number is an Euler number: 5, 61, 1385, ...). The source verified n ≤ 10 by computer and proved only transitivity. The proof is an induction on n: removing the last two elements embeds the action for n − 2, and a commutator of moves supported on different blocks isolates a 3-cycle; the group is primitive because a block containing one fibre is forced to be everything, so Jordan's theorem gives the alternating group; finally the second Bender–Knuth move is an odd permutation, by a sign recurrence through the tail fibres. Lean defines Z_n literally (an even-indexed element is below its neighbours), linear extensions as position-to-vertex bijections respecting the order, the Bender–Knuth move as the swap of adjacent positions when the two elements are incomparable (proved equivalent to the literal rule), and checks the counts 5 and 61 so that the statement cannot hold by an empty or trivial set.

title: Vanishing bounds for Romik's sequence $v(n)$ modulo odd prime powers
record_statement:
Let $p$ be a prime with $p\equiv3\pmod4$, let $e\ge1$, and let $(v(n))_{n\ge0}$ be the sequence defined in the paper. **The second conjecture.** If $e$ is odd, then

$$
v(n)\equiv0\pmod{p^e}
$$

for $n\ge\frac{(ep+2)(p+1)}{4}$. If $e$ is even, then

$$
v(n)\equiv0\pmod{p^e}
$$

for $n\ge\left\lceil\frac{ep^2}{4}\right\rceil$, with very few exceptions. Based on data with $n\le1500$, the listed exceptions are $(p,e)=(7,8),(7,24),(7,40),(11,36)$, whose correct lower bounds are respectively $102,298,494,1095$. The conjecture is an experimentally supported strengthening of the corresponding theorem.
source: Christian Krattenthaler and Thomas W. Müller, “The congruence properties of Romik's sequence of Taylor coefficients of Jacobi's theta function θ_3”, arXiv:2304.11471 (2024).
row_statement: The odd clause holds exactly as printed: for every prime p ≡ 3 (mod 4) and odd e, p^e divides v(n) for n ≥ (ep+2)(p+1)/4. For even e and n ≥ ⌈ep²/4⌉, the exceptions are classified exactly: p^e fails to divide v(n) if and only if e = (p+1)(2j+1) with 0 ≤ j < (p−1)/2 and 4n = ep² + (p+1) + 4r with 4r < p+1 and an explicit coefficient (r-th coefficient of a fixed polynomial over F_p) nonzero; at every exception v(n) misses by exactly one factor of p. The classification reproduces the source's four listed exceptions and corrected bounds, and shows the list is incomplete even within its own range (n ≤ 1500): (p,e) = (3,4) at n = 10 and (11,12) at n = 366–368. The source's own Theorem 17 is a factor of two weaker. The proof bounds the p-adic valuation of a square-root series within one factor of p, and supplies the last factor (odd e) or the exact failure set (even e) from a digit-level residue formula; the Lean proof obtains the residues mod p as coefficients of an explicit square root in characteristic p built from Frobenius. Lean defines v(n) by the source's recurrence (2.6) over ℚ, proves integrality, and checks the source's eleven printed values and its (7,8) data point.

title: Local weak convergence of random fullerenes to the planar hexagonal lattice
record_statement: Let $F_n$ be a random **fullerene**, meaning a finite, connected, 3-regular planar graph with faces of degrees both 5 and 6, chosen uniformly from the set of fullerenes with $n$ vertices. status_note: A9
title: The three-component-intersection extremal conjecture for odd n
record_statement:
Let $[n]=\{1,2,\ldots,n\}$ with $n$ odd, and let $\mathcal{F}$ be a family of graphs on $[n]$.

**Three-component-intersection conjecture.** If the intersection of any two graphs in $\mathcal{F}$ has at most three components, then

$$
|\mathcal{F}|\leq \frac{(n+3)^2}{8}\frac{1}{2^n}\cdot 2^{\binom{n}{2}}.
$$

For more than two components, the authors report that fixed-Hamilton-cycle constructions no longer appear optimal. For three components they suspect the bound is attained by a construction based on two half-sized cycles meeting at a point, although the displayed conjecture is the stated quantitative claim.
source: Imre Leader, Žarko Ranđelović and Ta Sheng Tan, “A Note on Hamiltonian-Intersecting Families of Graphs”, arXiv:2309.00757 (2023).
row_statement: For every h >= 1, on n = 6h-1 labelled vertices there is a family of (1+6h+12h^2)*2^(C(n,2)-6h) graphs whose pairwise intersections (including a graph with itself) have at most three components, exceeding the conjectured bound ((n+3)^2/8)*2^(C(n,2)-n); hence Leader-Randelovic-Tan Conjecture 7 fails for arbitrarily large odd n (ratio -> 4/3).

title: The second q-analogue of Liu's Dwork congruence
record_statement:
Let $m$ and $n$ be positive integers with $n\equiv1\;\allowbreak(\operatorname{mod}4)$ and $n>1$, and let $(a;q)_k$ denote the $q$-shifted factorial. **The q-analogue conjecture.**

$$
\sum_{k=0}^{mn-1}\frac{(1+q^{4k+1})(q^2;q^4)_k^3}{(1+q)(q^4;q^4)_k^3}q^k
\equiv \frac{[n]_{q^2}(q^3;q^4)_{(n-1)/2}}{(q^5;q^4)_{(n-1)/2}}q^{(1-n)/2}\sum_{k=0}^{m-1}\frac{(\frac12)_k^3}{k!^3}\;\allowbreak(\operatorname{mod}\Phi_n(q)^2).
$$

This is presented as a different q-analogue of the first case of Liu's supercongruence and as a refinement of an earlier congruence.
source: Victor J. W. Guo, “Dwork-type q-congruences through the q-Lucas theorem”, arXiv:2310.15207 (2023).
row_statement: The congruence holds for every m >= 1 and every n > 1 with n ≡ 1 (mod 4). Closest prior work: the block values in Guo's source, the base case from Guo and Zudilin (2020), and Guo's 2020 arbitrary-m result for n ≡ 3 (mod 4); the arbitrary-m statement modulo the square of the cyclotomic polynomial for n ≡ 1 (mod 4) was left open as Conjecture 6.2. The proof splits the left side into blocks of length n, shows that each block agrees with the right side's base value at every primitive n-th root of unity to first order (value and derivative), using a reciprocity under a shift of a parameter and a cancellation of the first-order shift errors between complementary blocks, and proves the base block by a terminating Dixon-type identity with an explicit WZ-style certificate. Lean works in the field of rational functions over Q with q the variable, states the congruence as coprimality of both denominators with Φ_n together with divisibility of the numerator of the difference by Φ_n^2, proves every denominator in the statement nonzero, and proves the base case rather than assuming it.

title: Intermediate-value conjecture for orientable total domination numbers
record_statement:
Let $G\in\mathcal{C}$ be a graph, and let ${\rm dom}_t(G)$ and ${\rm DOM}_t(G)$ denote its lower and upper orientable total domination numbers. For an orientation $f$ of $G$, write $G_f$ for the resulting oriented graph and $\gamma_t(G_f)$ for its total domination number. **Intermediate-value conjecture.** For every integer $c$ satisfying

$$
{\rm dom}_t(G)\leq c\leq {\rm DOM}_t(G),
$$

there exists an orientation $f$ of $G$ such that

$$
\gamma_t(G_f)=c.
$$

This extends the corresponding result known for complete graphs and complete bipartite graphs. The source attributes the conjecture to the authors of the cited earlier work, and no resolution is given here.
source: Sarah E. Anderson, Tanja Dravec, Daniel Johnston and Kirsti Kuenzel, “Orientable total domination in graphs”, arXiv:2311.16307 (2023).

row_statement: For every finite graph admitting an orientation of positive indegree at each vertex, every integer between the minimum and maximum attained total domination numbers is itself attained by such an orientation. title: Rational spherical triangle measurement conjecture
record_statement: Let a proper spherical triangle on the unit sphere have side lengths and area that are rational multiples of $\pi$, and let its measurement be the tuple $(E,a,b,c)$, with $a\le b\le c$. Define $\Lambda_1$ and $\Lambda_2$ as the sets of measurements given in the source. **Rational spherical triangle measurement conjecture.** The tuples in $\Lambda_1\cup\Lambda_2$ are the only measurements of proper rational spherical triangles. In particular, there are only finitely many measurements of proper rational spherical triangles with mutually distinct side lengths, namely, the seven measurements found by Little and Coxeter. This conjecture would classify all proper rational spherical triangles and implies that the mutually distinct-side cases are exactly the seven known examples.
source: Haiyang Wang, “Rational Spherical Triangles”, arXiv:2312.01633 (2023).

title: Preperiod conjecture for extensions of subtraction sets of size at most three
record_statement:
Let $A$ be a finite subtraction set with $|A|\leq 3$, let $S\in\{0,1\}^{\alpha}$ be a seed, and write $p=\operatorname{Per}(A,S)$. An integer of the form $kp+x$ is an **extension** of $A$ for every $k\in\mathbb{N}_+$ and $x\in A$ under the condition stated. **Preperiod-extension conjecture.** If $kp+x$ is an extension of $A$ for all $k\in\mathbb{N}_+$ and $x\in A$, then

$$
\operatorname{PrePer}(A,S)=0.
$$

The statement is the converse of the cited invariant-extension proposition for sets of size at most three. The source notes that it suffices to check $k=1$, and that the converse is not true for nonempty seeds in the unrestricted setting.
source: István Miklós and Logan Post, “Superpolynomial period lengths of the winning positions in the subtraction game”, arXiv:2312.02426 (2023).
row_statement: The conjecture holds: for a subtraction game with at most three moves and any seed, if p + x is an extension of the move set for every move x (p the period of the outcome sequence), then the outcome sequence is purely periodic. The source's extension criterion, applied at n + p, pulls the losing positions of the periodic tail backward into the start of the sequence; what remains is to exclude an extra early losing position. Such a position would force all of its forward neighbours to be winning in the periodic tail, and a new counting lemma (Lemma K: inclusion–exclusion on three translates of the set of losing residues, with matching singleton and pair counts and a pointwise triple inclusion) shows that this cannot happen when there are at most three moves. Lean proves the literal conjecture, the version with the hypothesis only for k = 1, a stronger pure-periodicity statement, and Lemma K; it also proves that the statement fails for four moves ({1,2,6,11}) and that Lemma K fails for {2,5,6,7}.

title: Odd-order graphs do not exhibit Laplacian perfect state transfer
record_statement: Let $X$ be a simple connected unweighted graph on an odd number of vertices. **Odd-order Laplacian PST conjecture.** Laplacian perfect state transfer does not occur in $X$. This extends the corresponding result for unweighted graphs on $3$ or $5$ vertices and follows for weighted join graphs under the additional assumption that the characteristic polynomial of the Laplacian has integer coefficients; the general case remains open.
source: Steve Kirkland and Hermie Monterde, “Quantum walks on join graphs”, arXiv:2312.06906 (2023).
row_statement: The conjecture of Kirkland and Monterde that Laplacian perfect state transfer does not occur in a simple connected unweighted graph of odd order is false. An explicit connected graph on 35 vertices has perfect state transfer between two vertices at time pi/2: two nonadjacent twin vertices u, v are joined to every vertex of a set W of 22 vertices, each vertex of W has 8 neighbours in a set R of 11 vertices, and each vertex of R has 16 neighbours in W. The Laplacian eigenvalues on the symmetric vector e_u + e_v are 0, 20 and 28, all divisible by 4, and the eigenvalue on e_u - e_v is 22, congruent to 2 modulo 4, so exp(i pi L / 2) maps e_u to e_v. The graph is the case k = 1 of a family of orders 36k^2 - 1 (r = 12k^2 - 1, c = 8k^2), proved on paper for all k. Lean checks the 35-vertex graph: it defines the conjecture for all simple connected graphs on an odd number of vertices with Mathlib's Laplacian and the complex matrix exponential, proves connectedness and the eigenvector identities by kernel computation, and derives the negation.

title: The general equality conjecture for $H(m,\alpha)$ and $H_2(m,\alpha)$
record_statement:
Let $H(m,\alpha)$ and $H_2(m,\alpha)$ be the quantities considered in the paper, with $m\geq 3$ and $\alpha\geq 2$, and define

$$
\lambda(\alpha)=\sum_{j=1}^{\infty}\frac{2^{j-1}}{\alpha^{2^j}}.
$$

**General equality conjecture.**

$$
H(m,\alpha)=H_{2}(m,\alpha)\quad\text{for all }m\geq 3\text{ and }\alpha\geq 2.
$$

In particular,

$$
\lim_{m\to\infty}\frac{2H(m,\alpha)}{m\alpha^m}=\lim_{m\to\infty}\frac{2H_{2}(m,\alpha)}{m\alpha^m}=\lambda(\alpha).
$$

This generalizes the conjectured equality at $\alpha=2$. The paper proves matching structural and asymptotic results for $H_2(m,\alpha)$, while the equality with $H(m,\alpha)$ is left open.
source: Wallace Peaslee, Attila Sali and Jun Yan, “An intermediate case of exponential multivalued forbidden matrix configuration”, arXiv:2312.11446 (2023).
row_statement: H(m, α) = H₂(m, α) for every m ≥ 3, and in fact for every α > 1: every triple-choice multigraph is matched or beaten in weight by a 2-recursive one. The source's edge-swap lemma gives only a closed vertex pair, and its Section 6 suggests combining closed sets without carrying it out. The proof normalizes cross-block edge weights by (α^{|A|}−1)(α^{|B|}−1) to force a closed pair of blocks, then uses size-weighted cloning and the convexity of α^x to homogenize the union without losing weight, iterating from singleton blocks. Lean defines triple-choice multigraphs, the weight, 2-recursiveness (Definition 1.3) and H, H₂ as maxima over nonempty finite sets, and checks small values (H(3,2) = 4, H(4,2) = 12 by exhausting all 81 choices, H₂(5,2) = 30, H₂(6,2) = 73) and that a non-2-recursive choice exists. The 'in particular' limit follows from the equality and the source's Theorem 6.2, which Lean does not formalize.

title: Parity congruence conjecture for finite Mordell--Tornheim sums
record_statement:
Let $r\in\N$, let $p$ be a prime, and let $\bfs\in\N^d$ satisfy $p>|\bfs|+1$, where $|\bfs|$ is the weight and $Z_{p^r}(\bfs)$ is the corresponding finite Mordell--Tornheim sum. **Finite Mordell--Tornheim congruence conjecture.** The following congruences should hold:

1. If $d=4$ and $|\bfs|$ is odd, then

$$
Z_{p^r}(\bfs)\equiv p^{2r-2}Z_p(\bfs)\pmod{p^{2r-1}}.
$$

2. If $d=4$ and $|\bfs|$ is even, then

$$
Z_{p^r}(\bfs)\equiv p^{r-1}Z_p(\bfs)\pmod{p^r}.
$$

3. If $d=5$ and $|\bfs|$ is even, then

$$
Z_{p^r}(\bfs)\equiv p^{2r-2}Z_p(\bfs)\pmod{p^{2r-1}}.
$$

In general, if $r\geq2$ and $d+|\bfs|$ is odd, then

$$
Z_{p^r}(\bfs)\equiv0\pmod{p^{2r-2}};
$$

if $r\geq2$ and $d+|\bfs|$ is even, then

$$
Z_{p^r}(\bfs)\equiv0\pmod{p^{r-1}}.
$$

The conjecture extends parity-dependent congruences for finite Mordell--Tornheim sums beyond the cases proved earlier in the paper. It is supported by extensive numerical evidence, while the stated general assertions remain open.
source: Crystal Wang and Jianqiang Zhao, “Mordell–Tornheim Zeta Values, Their Alternating Version, and Their Finite Analogs”, arXiv:2401.03380 (2024).
row_statement: All five assertions of Conjecture 3.4 of Wang and Zhao hold: for a prime p exceeding the weight plus one, every r >= 1 and every exponent vector s of positive integers, the finite sums Z_{p^r}^{d}(s) over compositions of p^r into d positive parts prime to p satisfy the stated divisibility by powers of p, the scaling laws in depths 4 and 5 relating level p^{r+1} to level p^r, and the general recurrence in r. Earlier work (Chen and Zhao; McCoy, Thielen, Wang and Zhao) treated only exponents all equal to 1, where just the last assertion applies; the source proved depth 3 by Bernoulli-number computations. The proof lifts the sum from level p^r to p^{r+1} keeping double precision (modulus p^{2r+1}), shows that the second moments of the carries vanish modulo p, and projects onto one reflection parity to gain a further factor of p. Lean states the sums and the five congruences literally in the integers modulo prime powers.

title: One-step separation conjecture for genus Tutte polynomials
record_statement:
Let $g$ be a positive integer, and let $\{M_i\}$ and $\{N_i\}$ be sequences of matroids. **One-step separation conjecture.** There exist two infinite sequences of matroids $\{M_i\}$ and $\{N_i\}$ such that

$$
T^{(g)}(M_i)=T^{(g)}(N_i)
$$

and

$$
T^{(g+1)}(M_i)\neq T^{(g+1)}(N_i).
$$

title: Linear-threshold conjecture for connected size Ramsey numbers of star matchings
record_statement:
Let $nK_{1,p}$ be the disjoint union of $n$ copies of the star $K_{1,p}$, and let $K_{1,m}$ be the star with $m$ edges. The connected size Ramsey number $\hat r_c(G_1,G_2)$ is the minimum number of edges in a connected graph $G$ such that $G\to (G_1,G_2)$. **Linear-threshold conjecture.** There exists a positive constant $c$ such that for all positive integers $m$, $n$, and $p$ with $m\geq c(n+p)$, we have

$$
\hat r_c(nK_{1,p},K_{1,m})=n(m+p)-1.
$$

The conjecture proposes that the exact value established in the paper for the stronger condition $m\geq (n^2+2pn+n-3)/2$ remains valid once $m$ is merely linear in $n+p$.
source: Fanghua Guo, Yanbo Zhang and Yunqing Zhang, “Matching-star size Ramsey numbers under connectivity constraint”, arXiv:2404.03175 (2024).
row_statement: For all positive integers n, p, m with m >= 5(n+p), the connected size Ramsey number of n vertex-disjoint stars K_{1,p} (red) against a star K_{1,m} (blue) equals n(m+p)-1: the minimum number of edges of a finite connected simple graph every red/blue edge colouring of which contains a red nK_{1,p} or a blue K_{1,m}. This proves the linear-threshold conjecture of Guo, Zhang and Zhang with c = 5; the source had the formula only for m >= (n^2+2pn+n-3)/2. Lean proves both the upper bound by construction and the lower bound for every connected graph with fewer edges. The constant 5 is not optimised; no constant c <= 2/3 can work (referee's computation at (n,p,m) = (2,1,2)).
adversarial_verdicts: PASS (candidates-review-R5-opus-20261119-r1/REVIEW-362603.md (Claude Opus 5.5, PASS, FLAGS none))
caveats: The constant 5 is not optimised. Bounded literature search only; the 2025 journal version still lists the conjecture as open. Two references the referee could not verify (arXiv:2606.04439, arXiv:2604.17356) were removed from the revised paper.

title: Polynomial formulas for truncated total depth in ordered trees
record_statement:
Let $n$ and $\ell$ be integers satisfying $n\geq \ell\geq 1$. Let $\operatorname{totalD}(n,k)$ denote the total quantity studied in the paper, and let $\operatorname{totalDTrunc}(n,k)$ denote its truncated version. For each $\ell$, let $a_{\ell}(n)$ and $b_{\ell}(n)$ be polynomials in $n$. **Polynomial-formula conjecture.** For all $n\geq \ell\geq 1$, \

$$
\operatorname{totalD}(n,2\ell-1)-\operatorname{totalDTrunc}(n,2\ell-1)=\frac{a_{\ell}(n)}{(n+2\ell+2)^{(2\ell-2)}}{2n \choose n-2\ell-1}
\
$$

 and \

$$
\operatorname{totalD}(n,2\ell)-\operatorname{totalDTrunc}(n,2\ell)=\frac{b_{\ell}(n)}{(n+2\ell+4)^{(2\ell-2)}}{2n+1 \choose n-2\ell-2}.
\
$$

 Here $a_{\ell}(n)$ and $b_{\ell}(n)$ have degree $2\ell-2$ and non-negative integer coefficients; the leading coefficient of $a_{\ell}(n)$ is $2\ell-1$, and the leading coefficient of $b_{\ell}(n)$ is $\ell$. The conjecture would provide a simplified expression for $\operatorname{totalDTrunc}(n,\ell)$, but the supplied text gives no resolution.
source: Stoyan Dimitrov, Martin Minchev and Yan Zhuang, “BFS versus DFS for fixed-level targets in ordered trees”, arXiv:2404.05664 (2026).
row_statement: For ordered trees with n edges and the depth-first-search scores totalD and totalDTrunc of Dimitrov, Minchev and Zhuang, for every l >= 1 there are polynomials a_l and b_l of degree 2l-2 with non-negative integer coefficients and leading coefficients 2l-1 and l such that, for all n >= l, totalD(n,2l-1) - totalDTrunc(n,2l-1) = a_l(n) C(2n, n-2l-1) / (n+2l+2)^(2l-2) and totalD(n,2l) - totalDTrunc(n,2l) = b_l(n) C(2n+1, n-2l-2) / (n+2l+4)^(2l-2), with rising factorials in the denominators. This is Conjecture 7.6 of arXiv v1. The proof is a binomial-sum enumeration of the score difference followed by a pairing argument for non-negativity. Lean also confirms that the quadratic coefficient of b_3 is 1133, where Table 3 of v1 prints 113.

status_note: replacement, accepted 111; fully literal lattice-theoretic formalization (32 modules); nearby framework arXiv:2512.20575 noted, not prior art
title: Orientation invariance conjecture for s-permutree lattices
record_statement:
Fix an $n$-tuple ${\boldsymbol{s}}$ of non-negative integers and a decoration map ${\boldsymbol{\delta}}$ assigning one of the four local orientations—none, up, down, or up-down—to each index $i$ with $s_i\ne0$. Let $W_{\boldsymbol{s}}/\equiv_{\boldsymbol{\delta}}$ be the ${\boldsymbol{\delta}}$-permutree lattice, and let its canonical join complex be the simplicial complex formed by canonical join representations.

**Orientation invariance conjecture for s-permutree lattices.** For fixed ${\boldsymbol{s}}$, changing any up decoration to a down decoration in ${\boldsymbol{\delta}}$ does not affect the cardinality of the ${\boldsymbol{\delta}}$-permutree lattice or the $f$-vector of its canonical join complex.

The conjecture concerns invariants that remain unchanged under the indicated decoration change, while the source notes that other structures, such as the undirected cover graph and face lattices, can depend on the positions of the up and down decorations. No resolution is supplied.
source: Eva Philippe and Vincent Pilaud, “Geometric realizations of the s-weak order and its lattice quotients”, arXiv:2405.02092 (2025).
row_statement: For every n, every tuple s of non-negative integers (zero entries allowed), every decoration of the other positions and every position k decorated up, changing the decoration at k from up to down changes neither the number of elements of the delta-permutree lattice (the quotient of the s-weak order by the lattice congruence generated by the decoration) nor, for any m, the number of faces of size m of its canonical join complex. This is Conjecture 76 of Philippe and Pilaud. Lean formalizes the objects literally: s-trees and their order with a proved lattice structure, s-arcs, the generated congruence (proved to contract exactly the forbidden arcs), the quotient lattice and canonical join representations defined lattice-theoretically; the proof identifies faces with marked arc diagrams by a sweep bijection and proves the forward direction of the source's Theorem 72 by a direct congruence construction.
adversarial_verdicts: PASS (shard016-candidate-review-opus-20261119-r1/REVIEW-362959.md (Claude Opus 5.5, PASS, FLAGS none; required the literal lattice-theoretic endpoint))
caveats: Bounded literature search only. A later paper on framing lattices (von Bell and Ceballos, arXiv:2512.20575) covers the s-weak order and classical permutree lattices but not s-permutree lattices or this conjecture; it suggests a possible alternative route that is not published. The case s = (1,...,1) is close to a known classical statement (Pilaud-Pons 2018, cardinality only).

title: The Jacobi-symbol conjecture for the integers $c_p$
record_statement:
Let $p$ be an odd prime. For $\delta\in\{0,1\}$, define

$$
D_p^{(\delta)}(w)=\left|\left(\frac{j^2-k^2}{p}\right)+\left(\frac{jk}{p}\right)w\right|_{\delta\leqslant j,k\leqslant(p-1)/2}-\left|\left(\frac{j^2-k^2}{p}\right)\right|_{\delta\leqslant j,k\leqslant(p-1)/2}.
$$

For $p\equiv1\pmod4$, let $c_p$ be the positive odd integer whose existence is asserted by the preceding theorem through $D_p^{(0)}(w)=-w((p-1)c_p/2)^2$; for $p\equiv3\pmod4$, let $c_p$ be the positive odd integer whose existence is asserted through $D_p^{(1)}(w)=w(c_p\sum_{k=1}^{(p-1)/2}(\frac{k}{p}))^2$.

**Jacobi-symbol conjecture for $c_p$.** For any odd prime $p$,

$$
\left(\frac{p}{c_p}\right)=1,
$$

where $(\frac{p}{c_p})$ is the Jacobi symbol.

The conjecture is based on numerical values of $c_p$ listed in the source. The supplied text gives no resolution or proof, so its status remains open.
source: Deyi Chen and Zhi-Wei Sun, “On determinants involving (j^2-k^2p) and (jkp)”, arXiv:2408.14401 (2024).
row_statement: For every odd prime p, let c_p be the positive odd integer defined by Chen and Sun's determinant identities (D_p^(0)(w) = -w((p-1)c_p/2)^2 for p = 1 mod 4; D_p^(1)(w) = w(c_p sum_{k<=(p-1)/2}(k/p))^2 for p = 3 mod 4). Then the Jacobi symbol (p / c_p) = 1 (Chen-Sun, arXiv:2408.14401, Conjecture 1.1); existence and uniqueness of c_p are part of the formal statement.
adversarial_verdicts: CLEARED (closecall-adjudication-A4-opus-20261119-r1, confidence 0.75)
caveats: Modest significance: the p = 1 mod 4 half uses a Ren-Luo-type Vandermonde reduction mod p; the new idea is in the p = 3 mod 4 half (c_p mod 4 via a Pfaffian sign congruence).
Orientation is (p / c_p) as in the source; (c_p / p) = 1 is false (e.g. p = 43, 47, 67).

title: Finiteness conjecture for connected graphs with odd metamour period
record_statement:
A graph's **metamour period** is the least positive integer $k$ for which its iterated metamour graph returns to the original graph, under the metamour operation used in the paper. Let $k$ range over the positive odd integers.

**Finiteness conjecture.** For each odd $k\in \mathbb{Z}^+$, there exist only finitely many connected graphs with metamour period $k$.

The paper has already classified the connected graphs with metamour period $3$: they are $C_7$ and $C_9$. The conjecture predicts analogous finiteness for every odd period, and the classification of such graphs remains open in general.
source: William Q. Erickson, Daniel Herden, Jonathan Meddaugh, Mark R. Sepanski, Mitchell Minyard and Kyle Rosengartner, “Limits and Periodicity of Metamour 2-Distance Graphs”, arXiv:2409.02306 (2024).
row_statement: For each positive odd integer k, there exists a finite collection of connected finite simple graphs whose least positive return to the identical labelled graph under repeated distance-exactly-two adjacency is k. Every connected finite simple graph of that exact period is isomorphic to a member of the list.

title: The complexity bound conjecture for S(e,23,e)-adic languages
record_statement:
Let $\mathcal{L}$ be an $S(e,23,e)$-adic language, and let $p_\mathcal{L}(n)$ denote its factor-complexity function.

**Complexity bound conjecture.** The complexity function $p_\mathcal{L}$ for any $S(e,23,e)$-adic language $\mathcal{L}$ satisfies

$$
p_\mathcal{L}(n) \leq 3n.
$$

This would extend the paper's classification of TRIP maps whose associated $S$-adic languages have complexity bounded above by $3n$ to the remaining map family $S(e,23,e)$ and its twins and conjugates.
source: Thomas Garrity and Otto Vaughn Osterman, “On the Factor Complexity Associated with a Family of Multidimensional Continued Fraction Algorithms”, arXiv:2410.02032 (2026).
row_statement: For every directive sequence over the two substitutions of the TRIP-map family S(e,23,e), the factor complexity of the S-adic language satisfies p(n) ≤ 3n for every n ≥ 1; the bound is attained. The source proves the analogous bound for the family (e,e,e), outlines the method for (e,23,e) in its Section 10 with Propositions 69–71 stated without proof, and names the remaining work: characterize the bispecial words and control their lengths. The proof does this: every double-Gauss block is a 3-free word followed by a single 3, which gives unique parsing and the exact extension sets in both directions (the source's Proposition 71, here proved); the bispecial factors are classified into 23 types; and a new cross-age matching between bispecials of different levels controls their total extension count. Lean defines the two substitutions, the directive applied with d(0) outermost as the source's Definition 14 requires, the language as the factor closure of all images, and the complexity as the number of factors of length n, and proves the bound for every directive sequence, including degenerate ones such as the all-S1 sequence.

title: The forbidden-pattern characterization conjecture for one-stack one-queue layouts
record_statement:
Let an ordered matching have a fixed non-separated layout. A **$1$-stack $1$-queue layout** uses one stack and one queue, and a **mixed layout on $1$ page** uses one page whose edges may be assigned to stacks or queues. The twelve and eight patterns referred to below are the patterns depicted in the source's figures.

**Forbidden-pattern characterization conjecture.** The ordered matching admits

$$
\text{a $1$-stack $1$-queue layout if and only if it avoids the 12 patterns depicted in the source's figure,}
$$

and admits a mixed layout on one page if and only if it avoids the 8 patterns depicted in the source's figure.

This conjecture proposes complete finite obstruction sets for the two smallest non-separated layout classes. It is consistent with the preceding computational enumeration of twelve and eight critical matchings, but the supplied source gives no proof or resolution.
source: Deborah Haun, Laura Merker and Sergey Pupyrev, “Forbidden Patterns in Mixed Linear Layouts”, arXiv:2412.12786 (2024).

row_statement: Both characterizations of Conjecture 31 hold for every finite ordered matching. The content is part (i): with the vertex order fixed, deciding a 1-stack 1-queue layout is a 2-SAT problem, whose contradiction cycles can be arbitrarily long, so 2-SAT alone gives no finite obstruction set. The proof shows that for intervals, three-edge forcing configurations plus propagation decide colourability, and that the geometry of intervals shortens every contradiction path to at most one link. Hence every matching without such a layout contains one with at most six edges, and an enumeration of the 11,465 matchings with at most six edges gives exactly the 12 patterns of Figure 19a. Part (ii) is routine (a failure needs a crossing pair and a nesting pair, at most four edges; also the source's Lemma 27). Lean defines ordered matchings on natural-number endpoints, layouts as the source does, and containment as an injective edge map preserving every endpoint comparison; the figure patterns are literal endpoint tables; no size cap enters the statement.

title: The derivation construction conjecture for transposed Poisson n-Lie algebras
record_statement:
Let $n\geq 2$ be an integer. Let $(L,\cdot,[\cdot,\ldots,\cdot])$ be a **transposed Poisson $n$-Lie algebra**, and let $D$ be a derivation of both $(L,\cdot)$ and $(L,[\cdot,\ldots,\cdot])$. Define an $(n+1)$-ary operation

$$
\mu(a_1,\ldots,a_{n+1})=\sum_{i=1}^{n+1}(-1)^{i-1}D(a_i)[a_1,\ldots,\hat{a}_i,\ldots,a_{n+1}],
$$

where $\hat{a}_i$ denotes omission of the $i$-th entry. **Derivation construction conjecture.** Then $(L,\cdot,\mu(\cdot,\ldots,\cdot))$ is a transposed Poisson $(n+1)$-Lie algebra. This conjecture extends the known construction for transposed Poisson 2-Lie algebras and addresses the open question of constructing and classifying simple transposed Poisson $n$-Lie algebras. Its validity for arbitrary $n\geq 2$ and the stated derivations remains open.
source: Farukh Mashurov, “On the transposed Poisson n-Lie algebras”, arXiv:2501.01714 (2025).
row_statement: The conjecture is false at n = 3 over every field of characteristic 0. The counterexample is a transposed Poisson 3-Lie algebra M₃ given by an explicit multiplication and bracket table, extended to polynomials in one variable t, with the derivation D = d/dt; the 4-ary operation μ built from D and the bracket fails the generalized Jacobi (Filippov) identity, with an explicit nonzero defect. The idea is that D = d/dt on the polynomial extension turns the Filippov defect of μ into a polynomial identity (a 'strong condition' whose first argument is itself a bracket) that would have to hold in the base algebra, and the table is chosen so that this degree-seven specialization is nonzero. Huang, Chen, Chen and Ding proved the construction for strong transposed Poisson n-Lie algebras, and Mashurov showed by a free-algebra computation that the strong condition can fail, without producing a counterexample to the construction. Lean states the conjecture with the bracket as a function with multilinearity and skew-symmetry hypotheses, over any field of characteristic 0, and proves its negation.

title: A q-analogue of the Van Hamme–Sun supercongruence equivalence
record_statement:
Let $n\equiv 1\pmod{4}$ be a positive integer. Define the $q$-integer $[m]=(1-q^m)/(1-q)$, the $q$-shifted factorial $(x;q)_k=(1-x)(1-xq)\cdots(1-xq^{k-1})$, and let $\Phi_n(q)$ denote the $n$-th cyclotomic polynomial. **q-analogue conjecture.**

$$
\sum_{k=0}^{n-1}(-1)^k[6k+1]\frac{(q;q^2)_k^3}{(q^4;q^4)_k^3}q^{3k^2} \equiv \sum_{k=0}^{n-1}(-1)^k[8k+1]\frac{(q;q^4)_k^3}{(q^4;q^4)_k^3}q^{2k^2+k} \pmod{[n]\Phi_n(q)^3}.
$$

This is a proposed $q$-analogue of an equivalence between two supercongruences for primes congruent to $1$ modulo $4$; its validity for all positive integers $n\equiv1\pmod4$ remains open.
source: Victor J. W. Guo and Chen Wang, “Refinements of Van Hamme's (E.2) and (F.2) supercongruences and two supercongruences by Swisher”, arXiv:2501.09626 (2025).
row_statement: The congruence holds modulo [n]Φ_n(q)³ for every positive n ≡ 1 (mod 4). The proof finds a common finite q-WZ recurrence for the two sides under the parameter shift a → aq⁴, with matching boundary terms, which gives divisibility of the difference by Φ_n(q)⁴ at every primitive n-th root of unity, and treats the proper divisors d of n (whose Φ_d divide [n]) by a separate cancellation. Lean states the congruence as divisibility of the numerator of the reduced difference by [n]Φ_n(q)³ in ℚ[q], proves the only denominator in the statement nonzero, includes the review's required statement verbatim, and proves that the difference is not zero at n = 5.

title: Kapranov–Schechtman's total-positivity conjecture for finite Coxeter groups
record_statement:
Let $(W,S)$ be a finite Coxeter group of rank $|S|=n$. For subsets $I,J\subset S$, let $W_I$ and $W_J$ be the parabolic subgroups of $W$ of types $I$ and $J$, respectively. Define the metamatrix $M(W)=(M_{pq})_{0\leq p,q\leq n}$ by

$$
M_{pq}=\sum_{I,J\subset S,|I|=p,|J|=q}|W_I\backslash W/W_J|.
$$

**Kapranov–Schechtman's conjecture.** The metamatrix $M(W)$ is totally positive.

This extends the known type-$A$ result, where $W=S_n$, to arbitrary finite real reflection groups. The conjecture is proved in the source for type $B$ and the exceptional types, while the general finite-Coxeter-group case remains open.
source: Zhentao Wang, Jiawen Xie and Xuhang Zhang, “On the Total Positivity of Contingency Metamatrices”, arXiv:2503.02213 (2025).
row_statement: The conjecture fails for the Coxeter group of type D_27: the 16×16 submatrix of M(D_27) with rows p = 0..15 and columns q = 12..27 has negative determinant (a 372-digit integer), so M(D_27) is not totally positive, not even totally nonnegative. The source proves the conjecture for type B and the exceptional types and does no type-D computation; every rank from 2 to 26 is totally positive (reproduced independently by two lanes, not formalized and not claimed), so no small-rank check finds the failure. The proof identifies parabolic subgroups with stabilizers of face vectors, counts double cosets by Burnside's lemma through fixed-face counts with a type-D gluing identity (Stembridge's fixed-face data are the closest prior work), and turns the result into an explicit integer formula for every entry. Lean works with the concrete group of even signed permutations of 27 coordinates and its 27 standard reflections (the D_27 fork), defines parabolics as generated subgroups and entries as Nat.card of Mathlib's double-coset quotient, proves the formula, evaluates all 256 entries of the minor in the kernel (decide +kernel, no native_decide), and certifies the sign of the determinant by an integer triangular factorization.

title: Sign-change conjecture for Birch–Erdős representation functions
record_statement:
Let $f_{p,q}(n)$ be the Birch–Erdős representation function, with $p$ and $q$ relatively prime integers satisfying $q>p>2$. **Sign-change conjecture.** The sign of

$$
f_{p,q}(n+1)-f_{p,q}(n)
$$

changes infinitely often. The conjecture is presented as a possible example of the Chebyshev bias phenomenon; the source does not establish it.
source: Yuchen Ding, Honghu Liu and Zi Wang, “Note on a theorem of Birch and Erdős”, arXiv:2503.11676 (2025).
row_statement: The conjecture holds: for all coprime q > p > 2, the difference f_{p,q}(n+1) − f_{p,q}(n) is strictly positive for infinitely many n and strictly negative for infinitely many n, where f_{p,q}(n) counts the representations of n as a sum of distinct numbers p^a q^b. Infinitely many increases follow from the authors' Corollary 3 (f is unbounded). The new part is the decreases: if f were eventually nondecreasing, a comparison at roots of unity would force certain twisted products over pure powers to vanish, while the exact product over all roots of unity gives a uniform lower bound; the contradiction needs p > 2 (for p = 2 the authors prove that f is monotone). Lean defines f by the source's literal representation count and proves both infinitely many strict increases and infinitely many strict decreases, with non-vacuity checks.

title: The uri multiplicity threshold shuffle conjecture
record_statement:
Let $\mathcal{C}$ be the set of compositions, let $\ell(\boldsymbol{\alpha})$ be the length of a composition, and let $\operatorname{ind}_a(\boldsymbol{\alpha})$ be its index at $a$. Define the uri multiplicities by

$$
\mu_{a,\boldsymbol{\alpha}}=B_1(\ell(\boldsymbol{\alpha}),\operatorname{ind}_a(\boldsymbol{\alpha})),
$$

where

$$
B_1(m,n)=\frac{1}{m!}\sum_{k=0}^{n-1}\binom{m}{k}B_k.
$$

**Uri multiplicity threshold shuffle conjecture.** The uri multiplicities satisfy the threshold shuffle identities from the source's definition. The supplied text gives no resolution status for these identities.
source: Annika Burmester and Ulf Kühn, “On post-Lie structures for free Lie algebras”, arXiv:2504.19661 (2025).
row_statement: The uri multiplicities satisfy threshold shuffle identity (i) of the source's Definition A.5 in full, and identity (ii) whenever the middle composition τ is nonempty; identity (ii) as printed, with no condition on τ, is false (at σ = τ = ∅, ϑ = (1), d₁ = d₂ = 0 it would assert 0 = −1). The corrected statement is what the source needs: the proof of its Theorem 5.11 uses (i) for adjacent factors and (ii) for factors separated by a nonempty word, its Example A.6(ii) follows that split, and the normalized solutions of its Remark A.8 are incompatible with the printed empty case. The proof expands the multiplicities over the cuts of a word, uses the compatibility of shuffle with deconcatenation and a divided-difference identity for the Bernoulli-type numbers B₁(m, n), and cancels the remaining alternating sum over cuts of the middle word, which is where τ ≠ ∅ enters. Lean states Definition A.5 and the multiplicities literally (with multiplicity 0 at non-positive thresholds, which implements the omission of inadmissible insertions), proves (i), proves (ii) for τ ≠ ∅, proves the counterexample to the printed (ii), and reproduces both parts of the source's Example A.6.

title: Switch-generation conjecture for the matching preorder
record_statement:
Let $\mathcal{M}_n$ be the set of the labelled perfect matchings under consideration, and let $\preceq$ be the preorder on this set. A **switch** is the local transformation defined earlier in the paper. **Switch-generation conjecture.** If $N,M\in\mathcal{M}_n$ satisfy $N\preceq M$, then there exists a sequence

$$
N=M_1\preceq M_2\preceq\dots\preceq M_{k-1}\preceq M_k=M
$$

such that $M_j$ is a switch of $M_{j+1}$ for every $j$. This is presented as an open conjecture about whether the preorder is generated by switches; the supplied parser gives no evidence of resolution.
source: Joseph Briggs, Jessica McDonald and Songling Shan, “Degree sequences realizing labelled perfect matchings”, arXiv:2510.01110 (2025).
row_statement: For perfect matchings N and M of the vertex set {1, ..., n}, write N ⪯ M when every weakly decreasing degree sequence that has a realization containing M also has one containing N. If N ⪯ M then there is a chain N = M_1 ⪯ M_2 ⪯ ... ⪯ M_k = M in which each step is one of the three switches of the source. This is Conjecture 11 of Briggs, McDonald and Shan. The proof shows that the preorder is the reverse Bruhat order on fixed-point-free involutions: a new separating-graph lemma produces, whenever a crossing-count inequality fails, a degree sequence realized with M but not with N; a direct induction on rank defects then moves from N toward M one switch at a time, and the source's Lemma 10(b) keeps every step inside the preorder. Lean defines matchings as edge sets, realizability by actual simple graphs with prescribed degrees, and the three switch types literally.

title: Existence of regular open and closed XOR-magic graphs of power-of-two order
record_statement:
Let $n$ be a positive integer, and let $d$ be a degree. An **open XOR-magic graph** and a **closed XOR-magic graph** are graphs admitting, respectively, an open or closed XOR-magic labeling. The graphs below are required to have order $2^n$.

For each degree

$$
d\in\{5,7,\ldots,2^n-7,2^n-5\},
$$

there exists a $d$-regular open XOR-magic graph of order $2^n$. For each degree

$$
d\in\{4,6,\ldots,2^n-6,2^n-4\},
$$

there exists a $d$-regular closed XOR-magic graph of order $2^n$.

**Existence conjecture.** For every permitted degree $d$ in the two displayed sets, the corresponding regular open or closed XOR-magic graph exists. This would complete the existence picture apart from the degrees excluded by the previously stated nonexistence result and extend the constructions known for order $16$ and order $8$ to every order that is a power of two.

title: The minimum-fort-size conjecture for marginal observances
record_statement:
Let $G$ be a graph. Write $\underline{f}(G)$ for the minimum fort size of $G$, let $\mathrm{MObs}(G;i)$ denote the marginal observance at step $i$, and let $\gamma_P(G)$ denote the power domination number. For a positive integer $k$, write $[k]=\{1,\ldots,k\}$. **Minimum-fort-size conjecture.** If

$$
\underline{f}(G)\geq 4,
$$

then

$$
\mathrm{MObs}(G;i)\geq 4
$$

for all $i\in[\gamma_P(G)]$. This asks whether the relationship between minimum fort size and marginal observances established for smaller minimum fort sizes extends to minimum fort size at least four; its status is not resolved in the source.
source: Beth Bjorkman, Sean English and Johnathan Koch, “Cost-Benefit Analysis for PMU Placement in Power Grids”, arXiv:2601.19775 (2026).
row_statement: The conjecture that minimum fort size at least 4 forces every marginal observance MObs(G;i), for i up to the power domination number, to be at least 4 is false. An explicit graph on 25 vertices, built from two copies of the Fano plane with two lines removed joined through a hub, has no fort of size at most 3, maximum observed-set sizes 11 and 14 with one and two sensors, and power domination number at least 3, so its second marginal observance is 3. (By the referee's computation the maximum observances are 0, 11, 14, 19, 25 and the power domination number is 4.) A generic random search over about 80 million graphs on 10 to 28 vertices found no counterexample; the witness comes from a structured construction.

title: The shift-additivity conjecture for periodic binary sequences
record_statement: Let $n$ be a positive integer, let $c\geq \left\lceil\frac{n}{2}\right\rceil$, and let $d=n-c$. Let $\mathcal{B}(n,c,d)$ denote the specified class of binary sequences, let $R^b(\mathbf{s}_n)$ denote the $b$-fold shift of $\mathbf{s}_n$, and let $\operatorname{add}(\mathbf{s}_n)$ denote its additivity parameter. Suppose that $0<b<n$ and that, for some $d_2$, $R^b(\mathbf{s}_n)\in\mathcal{B}(n,c,d_2)$ with $\operatorname{add}(R^b(\mathbf{s}_n))>\operatorname{add}(\mathbf{s}_n)$. **Shift-additivity conjecture.** Then $b=d_2$. The conjecture would extend the statements of the cited proposition and corollary from $c\geq\left\lceil\frac{2n-1}{3}\right\rceil$ to $c\geq\left\lceil\frac{n}{2}\right\rceil$, allowing the same conclusions about the unique relevant shift and the nonlinear complexity of the associated periodic sequence; the source reports experimental evidence but says that the proposed technique does not prove it.
source: Qin Yuan, Chunlei Li and Xiangyong Zeng, “The structure and enumeration of periodic binary sequences with high nonlinear complexity”, arXiv:2602.01134 (2026).
row_statement: The conjecture holds in its full range c ≥ ⌈n/2⌉. The source's Lemma 7 and Corollary 1 give b = d₂ when the two spacings and the two additivity parameters satisfy an inequality, which covers c ≥ ⌈(2n−1)/3⌉, and the authors say that their technique does not reach further. The new tool is a Run Lemma about the multiset of lengths of zero runs of the cyclic difference word of a sequence in the class B(n, c, d): comparing these run lengths before and after the shift handles the overlap that the published argument leaves open, and a reflection argument on cyclic windows finishes the proof. Lean states the source's Definitions 2 and 3 and the shift R^b literally for sequences Fin n → Bool, includes the membership of the original sequence in B(n, c, n − c) that the MathDB paraphrase leaves implicit, proves that the additivity parameter exists and is unique on the class, and proves the conjecture; it also shows by an example that the strict inequality in the hypothesis is needed.

title: Completeness conjecture for regular Inverse Treblecross positions
record_statement:
Let $R$ be the regular set of board states, let a state have at most one piece, and let $\mathcal{G}$ denote its Sprague–Grundy value. **Completeness conjecture.** The regular set $R$ contains all board states that possess at most one piece and satisfy $\mathcal{G} \le 1$, with exactly four isolated exceptions:

$$
[1 X 1],\quad [1 X 4],\quad [4 X 1],\quad \text{and}\quad [4 X 4].
$$

These four states are described as isolated anomalies, and empirical data indicates that all other sufficiently long states in their residue classes have $\mathcal{G}>1$; the completeness of $R$ beyond the stated exceptions remains unproved.
source: Kai Liang and Muxi Li, “A Weak Solution of Inverse Treblecross”, arXiv:2604.16759 (2026).
row_statement: The conjecture (as printed in version 1 of the source, which the MathDB record follows) holds: among boards of Inverse Treblecross with at most one X, those with Sprague–Grundy value at most 1 are exactly the boards of the regular set R together with [1X1], [1X4], [4X1] and [4X4], and each of these four has value exactly 1 and lies outside R. The source computes the values on R and tabulates small cases; what was missing is that no other board, of any length, has value at most 1. Mixed-residue cases are settled in two moves from the source's values for empty boards. When both gaps lie in the critical residue classes, a move at distance four supplies the missing option once the values of an auxiliary family of two-piece boards are known, and those are certified by a coupled induction: a finite abstract-interpretation certificate (each gap known exactly when small, otherwise by its residue modulo 10) checked for all gap lengths at once. Lean defines the game literally on lists of Booleans (a move fills an empty cell without creating three adjacent X's; the value is the mex of the option values), proves the certificate checker sound, proves that the certificate covers every concrete gap length, and proves the classification.

title: Generalized reflectional periodicity conjecture for odd Inverse k-cross games
record_statement:
Let $k=2m+1$ with $m\geq1$, and consider an Inverse $k$-cross game with empty-board state $[a]$. Let $\mathcal{G}([a])$ denote its Sprague–Grundy value, and let $\oplus$ denote nim-sum. **Generalized reflectional periodicity conjecture.** For every such game, $\mathcal{G}([a])\leq1$, and

$$
\mathcal{G}([2+3m+a])=\mathcal{G}([a])\oplus(m\bmod2),
$$

$$
\mathcal{G}([2+5m-a])=\mathcal{G}([a])\oplus(m\bmod2).
$$

For $k=2$, eventual periodicity is known through the identification with Dawson's Kayles, whereas for even $k>2$ eventual periodicity is unknown; the asserted uniform bound and reflectional periodicity for odd constraints remain conjectural.
source: Kai Liang and Muxi Li, “A Weak Solution of Inverse Treblecross”, arXiv:2604.16759 (2026).
row_statement: The conjecture holds, and more is true: for every odd k = 2m+1 the Sprague–Grundy value of the empty board of length n is (n + [n mod (3m+2) ≥ k]) mod 2. With P = 3m+2, either player can force the game to end with exactly 2⌊n/P⌋ + [n mod P ≥ k] empty cells, even when one extra nim-heap of size one is added: the board is cut into blocks of k + (m+1) cells, each containing m+1 disjoint supports and only m high cells, and the defender answers inside the block the opponent just played in. So the length of the game is fixed and its parity gives the value; the bound G ≤ 1 and both identities follow from the formula. Lean defines the game on the sets of unmarked cells (a position is legal when every window of k cells contains an unmarked cell), the options and the Sprague–Grundy value as a minimum excluded value, proves the three statements of the conjecture and the closed formula for every m ≥ 0, and proves that the moves of this model are, move for move, the placements of the source's game on a Boolean board.

title: Lattice-realization conjecture for preorder lattice-point posets
record_statement:
Let $\tau$ be a preorder of size $n$, let $P_\tau$ be its lattice-point poset, let $M_{P_\tau}(x,y)$ be its $M$-triangle, and let $\overline{M}_{P_\tau}$ be the transmutation defined by

$$
\overline f(x,y)=f\left(\frac{1-y}{1-xy},1-xy\right).
$$

**Lattice-realization conjecture.** There exists a finite graded lattice $L_\tau$ of rank $n$ such that

$$
\mathcal Z(P_\tau,t)=\mathcal Z(L_\tau,t),\qquad \overline M_{P_\tau}(x,y)=M_{L_\tau}(x,y).
$$

In particular, the rank-generating polynomial of $L_\tau$ equals $h(\tau,t)$. The conjecture extends the arbor setting; the source gives examples for chain preorders but no general resolution.
source: Frédéric Chapoton and Christos A. Athanasiadis, “Polytopes and posets associated to preorders”, arXiv:2605.26916 (2026).
row_statement: For the three-element preorder with two incomparable minima below one maximum, no finite graded lattice of rank three has M-triangle equal to the rational transmutation of the M-triangle of the preorder polytope's lattice-point poset. This refutes Conjecture 8.1.
lean_vs_paper: Lean checks the native rank and transmutation obstruction for the three-element corolla. The written proof extends it to every corolla with at least two leaves and discusses the opposite corolla and zeta polynomial.

title: Conjectural interval-family homomorphisms from dihedral type to type A
record_statement:
Let $1\le b\le a<n-1$ and $a>1$. For the type-$A$ braid monoid, write $w_0^{[r,s]}$ for the longest element of the parabolic subgroup on the interval $[r,s]$.

**Interval-family homomorphism conjecture.** The assignments

$$
\widehat{T}_1\mapsto T_{w_0^{[1,a]}},\qquad \widehat{T}_2\mapsto T_{w_0^{[b,n-1]}}
$$

define a homomorphism $\operatorname{Br}^+(I_2(N))\to\operatorname{Br}^+_n$ if one of the following holds:

$$
N=\frac{2n}{n+b-a-2}\in2\mathbb Z_{>0};
$$

$$
a+b=n\quad\text{and}\quad N=\frac{n}{b-1}\in1+2\mathbb Z_{>0};
$$

$$
a+1=2(b-1),\quad a+b<n,\quad\text{and}\quad N=6.
$$

The paper presents these as a conjectural infinite family of non-disjoint standard homomorphisms and reports verification for $n\le15$.
source: Arkady Berenstein, Jacob Greenstein and Jian-Rong Li, “Artin monoids, their homomorphisms and twins”, arXiv:2606.26776 (2026).
row_statement: The conjecture holds in all three cases and for every n: the two half twists (positive lifts of the longest elements on the intervals [1,a] and [b,n−1]) satisfy the braid relation of length N in the positive braid monoid, so they define a monoid homomorphism from the dihedral Artin monoid Br⁺(I₂(N)). Cases I and II follow from a periodic-braid identity: rotation and overlap identities for half twists, proved by positive rewriting. Case III (N = 6) comes from a seven-move identity on four strands, transported to all sizes by cabling with strands of unequal width. The source proves the subfamilies N = 3 (of case II) and N = 4, b ≥ 2 (of case I) and reports computer verification for n ≤ 15. Lean works in the presented positive monoid on σ₁, …, σ_{n−1} with the braid and commutation relations, defines the half twists as explicit triangular positive words, and proves both the alternating relation and the existence of the homomorphism with no premise beyond the conjecture's hypotheses; an earlier group-level proof is kept.

title: Uniqueness of terminal transversals under $(213)\rightarrow(123)$ moves
record_statement: Let $Y$ be the Young diagram under consideration, let $S_Y$ denote its transversals, and let $S_Y(213)$ denote the transversals avoiding the pattern $(213)$. For a transversal $T\in S_Y$, consider sequences of $(213)\rightarrow(123)$ moves, each replacing an occurrence of the pattern $(213)$ by $(123)$. **Uniqueness conjecture.** Starting with a transversal $T\in S_Y$, all sequences of $(213)\rightarrow(123)$ moves terminate in the same transversal $T'\in S_Y(213)$. This is a confluence assertion for the pattern moves and would make the $(213)$-avoiding terminal transversal canonically determined by the starting transversal. The supplied text does not indicate whether the assertion has been proved or remains open.
source: Zvezdelina Stankova, “Shape-Wilf-ordering of permutations of length 3”, arXiv:math/0609644 (2006).
row_statement: For every finite Young diagram with a transversal, rectangle-contained 213→123 swaps starting from that transversal have no infinite chain, and any two reachable transversals have a common descendant. There is exactly one reachable 213-avoiding transversal, attained by a finite maximal sequence, and every finite maximal sequence ends there.

title: The strengthened 2-criticality conjecture for row-isotoped abelian 2-groups
record_statement:
Let $L_s$ be the latin square of order $n=2^s$, and let $\alpha_{k,k'}$ be the row isotopism that interchanges rows $k$ and $k'$ and fixes every other row. Suppose that

$$
\left|k-k'\right|<3.
$$

**Strengthened 2-criticality conjecture.** The set $\operatorname{gcs}(\alpha_{k,k'}L_s)$ is 2-critical and strong, and completes top down to $\alpha_{k,k'}L_s$.

The theorem preceding this conjecture proves the claim under the additional hypothesis that $k$ and $k'$ lie among four consecutive indices beginning at a multiple of $4$. The authors expect that this stronger version remains true when that additional condition is weakened, but no resolution is given here.
source: Carlo Hamalainen, “New 2–critical sets in the abelian 2–group”, arXiv:math/0612338 (2006).
row_statement: The conjecture holds for every order 2^s and every pair of rows less than three apart, for the greedy order that the source describes in words and uses throughout (bottom row first, right to left). For each such swap the greedy critical set is given by explicit blank-cell masks written in binary across block boundaries; each clue is the lexicographically least cell of a private intercalate, which gives 2-criticality, and in each row the blanks are forced one at a time along an acyclic forcing graph, which gives strong completion and top-down completion. The source proved the case where both rows lie in an aligned block of four (its Theorem 5.1) and checked the rest by computer through order 32; the new cases are the swaps that cross a block boundary, of which the odd adjacent ones are easy and the two distance-two families carry the substance. title: The Catalan triangle Laurent polynomial and positivity conjecture
record_statement:
Let $n_1,\ldots,n_m,n_{m+1}=n_1$ be positive integers. For an integer $j$ and non-negative integers $a,r$ with $a\leqslant n_1$, consider

$$
\frac{1}{[n_m+a]}{n_1+n_m\brack n_1-a}^{-1}\sum_{k=a}^{n_1}[2k][k]^{2r}q^{jk^2-(r+1)k}\prod_{i=1}^{m}{n_i+n_{i+1}\brack n_i+k}.
$$

**Catalan triangle Laurent polynomial and positivity conjecture.** This expression is a Laurent polynomial in $q$, and it has non-negative integer coefficients when $0\leqslant j\leqslant m$. This is presented as a stronger version of Theorem and as a generalization of a conjecture attributed to Guo and Wang; the supplied span does not state whether it has since been resolved.
source: Victor J. W. Guo and Xiuguo Lian, “Proofs of two conjectures on Catalan triangle numbers”, arXiv:1806.02685 (2018).
row_statement: For positive integers n_1,...,n_m with n_{m+1}=n_1, every integer j, and nonnegative integers a, r with a <= n_1, the expression (1/[n_m+a]) [n_1+n_m choose n_1-a]_q^{-1} sum_{k=a}^{n_1} [2k][k]^{2r} q^{jk^2-(r+1)k} prod_{i=1}^m [n_i+n_{i+1} choose n_i+k]_q is a Laurent polynomial in q with integer coefficients, and its coefficients are nonnegative when 0 <= j <= m (Guo-Lian, arXiv:1806.02685, Conjecture 6.1; MathDB 381408 = 339461).

title: Cardoso–Luz conjecture on adverse graphs
record_statement:
An **adverse graph** is a graph $H$ without isolated vertices such that $upsilon(H)$ and $lambda_{min}(H)$ are integers, and, for every vertex $i\in V(H)$,

$$
\upsilon(H-N_H(i))=\upsilon(H),\qquad \lambda_{min}(H-N_H(i))=\lambda_{min}(H).
$$

Here $upsilon(H)$ is the optimal value of the quadratic stability-number bound and $lambda_{min}(H)$ is the least eigenvalue of $H$. A graph is a **$\mathcal{Q}$-graph** when it belongs to the class $\mathcal{Q}$ defined in the paper.

**Cardoso–Luz conjecture.** All adverse graphs are $\mathcal{Q}$-graphs.

Computational tests with adverse graphs supported the conjecture, but it remains open. Its resolution would clarify the polynomial-time recognition of $\mathcal{Q}$-graphs.
source: Domingos M. Cardoso, “A survey on graphs with convex quadratic stability number”, arXiv:1811.05516 (2018).

title: Exact formula conjecture for the rainbow-saturation coefficient
record_statement:
For each integer $k\geq 4$, let $f(k)$ be the auxiliary extremal function from the paper and let $\alpha_{k+2}$ be the coefficient in the asymptotic formula for rainbow saturation, so that $\operatorname{sat}(n,\mathcal{R}(K_{k+2}))=\alpha_{k+2}n+O(1)$. **Exact coefficient conjecture.** For every $k\geq 4$,

$$
\alpha_{k+2}=f(k)=k+\left\lceil\frac{-1+\sqrt{4k-3}}{2}\right\rceil.
$$

This conjecture is proposed as a way to close the gap between the lower and upper bounds for rainbow saturation by determining the auxiliary function $f(k)$ exactly. The supplied text does not state whether it has been resolved.
source: Debsoumya Chakraborti, Kevin Hendrey, Ben Lund and Casey Tompkins, “Rainbow saturation for complete graphs”, arXiv:2212.04640 (2024).

title: The local reversal edge conjecture for characteristic imset polytopes
record_statement:
Let $\mathcal{G}$ be a directed acyclic graph with skeleton $G$, and let $i$ be a vertex. Define $\mathcal{G}_{\downarrow i}$ by orienting every edge between $i$ and a neighbor toward $i$, while leaving all other edges as in $\mathcal{G}$. Write $c_\mathcal{G}$ and $c_{\mathcal{G}_{\downarrow i}}$ for their characteristic imsets, and let $\CIM_G$ denote the characteristic imset polytope associated with $G$. **Local reversal edge conjecture.** If $\mathcal{G}$ and $\mathcal{G}_{\downarrow i}$ are not Markov equivalent, then

$$
\operatorname{conv}\left(c_\mathcal{G},c_{\mathcal{G}_{\downarrow i}}\right)
$$

is an edge of $\CIM_G$. A linear bound on the diameter of $\CIM_G$ would follow from this conjecture; the source establishes quadratic bounds in general and linear bounds for trees and for the whole polytope, but does not resolve the conjecture for arbitrary skeletons.
source: Petter Restadh, “Diameters of the Characteristic Imset Polytopes”, arXiv:2302.03647 (2023).
row_statement: There is a five-vertex DAG C with eight arrows for which making vertex 4 a sink (one-based numbering) yields a DAG D on the same skeleton that is not Markov equivalent to C. title: The affine type B distance conjecture
record_statement:
Let $w$ be an affine signed permutation in $\widetilde{S}^B_n$. An integer $j\in[n-1]$ is **good** if $w$ restricts to a bijection from $\pm[j]$ to itself, and it is **very good** if this restriction is an even-signed permutation. Define

$$
\operatorname{bl}^{\widetilde{C}}(w)=1+\#\{\text{good values for }w\},\qquad \operatorname{bl}^{\widetilde{B}}(w)=1+\#\{\text{very good values for }w\}.
$$

Here $\$(w)$ and $\operatorname{dis}(w)$ denote the quantities defined for affine signed permutations in the paper. **The affine type B conjecture.** If $w\in\widetilde{S}^B_n$, then

$$
\$(w)=\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{dis}(w)+\operatorname{bl}^{\widetilde{C}}(w)-\operatorname{bl}^{\widetilde{B}}(w).
$$

This conjecture extends the finite-type formula to affine type $\widetilde{B}$. If true, it would imply $\$(w)-\operatorname{dis}(w)/2\leq n$ for all $w\in\widetilde{S}^B_n$; the corresponding boundedness behavior is contrasted with the affine type $\widetilde{D}$ case.
source: Joel Brewster Lewis and Bridget Eileen Tenner, “Bargain hunting in a Coxeter group”, arXiv:2302.04404 (2023).
row_statement: The conjecture holds for every n: the cheapest way to write an affine signed permutation w of type B as a product of reflections of that group, where a reflection costs its depth, costs dis(w)/2 + bl_C(w) − bl_B(w). Lower bound: every reflection changes the displacement by at most twice its cost, and a crossing-count lemma shows that each good cut that is not very good (an odd block) forces one extra unit of cost, because a product of reflections of the type B group restricted to a block that is preserved by all of them has an even number of sign changes. Upper bound: a greedy rule that always applies an efficient swap, and switches the partner of the swap whenever the obvious choice would close an odd block, reaches the identity at exactly that cost; its termination and invariants are proved. The source proves the analogous formulas where no branching occurs and in finite type D; in affine type B no depth formula was available. Lean defines the group as permutations of the integers with the periodicity, negation and parity conditions, takes costs over lists of reflections each of which belongs to the group, and proves that the doubled formula dis(w) + 2(bl_C(w) − bl_B(w)) is the least element of the set of doubled costs, so the minimum is attained.

title: Ilinca–Kahn conjectured bipartite matching entropy bound
record_statement:
Let $G$ be a bipartite graph on $X\cup Y$ with $|X|=\ell$ and $|Y|=M\geq \ell$. For each $x\in X$, let $d_x$ be its degree, and define

$$
\psi(d,t)=t^{-1}\bigl[\log d!-\log \Gamma(d-t+1)\bigr],
$$

where $\Gamma$ is the usual gamma function. Let $\Phi_\ell(G)$ denote the number of matchings of size $\ell$ in $G$.

**Ilinca–Kahn conjectured matching bound.** If, for each $x\in X$, $t_x=\ell d_x/M$, then

$$
\log\Phi_\ell(G)\leq \sum_{x\in X}\psi(d_x,t_x).
$$

This proposed inequality is a precise version of an earlier entropy bound discussed in the paper. The source proposes it as a conjecture and does not provide a proof or resolution.
source: Liviu Ilinca and Jeff Kahn, “Asymptotics of the Upper Matching Conjecture”, arXiv:1205.4342 (2012).

title: The domination-number conjecture for total graphs of finite rings
record_statement:
Let $R$ be an arbitrary ring with Jacobson radical $J$, and suppose that

$$
R/J=M_{n_1}(F_1) \times \ldots \times M_{n_k}(F_k),
$$

where each $F_i$ is a finite field and $n_i\geq 2$ for all $i$. For a finite ring $A$, let $\tau(A)$ denote its total graph and let $\gamma(\tau(A))$ denote the domination number of that graph. **Domination-number conjecture.**

$$
\gamma(\tau(R))=\min_i\{n_i(|F_i|-1)+1\}.
$$

The preceding theorem establishes the corresponding upper bound without the restrictions $n_i\geq 2$. The examples of $M_2(\mathbb{Z}_2)$ and $M_3(\mathbb{Z}_2)$ attain this bound, while factors with $n_i=1$ can give a strictly smaller domination number; the equality in the stated generality is therefore proposed but not established here.
source: David Dolžan and Polona Oblak, “The total graphs of finite rings”, arXiv:1401.1941 (2014).
acceptance_record: not in ledger (round 2; pipeline complete; see packet)
row_statement: The conjecture of Dolzan and Oblak that the total graph of a ring R with R/J a product of matrix rings M_{n_i}(F_i), n_i >= 2, has domination number min_i (n_i(|F_i| - 1) + 1) is false: for R = M_2(F_3) the formula predicts 5, but the four matrices 0 and E12 + E21 + c E22 (c in F_3) dominate the total graph, so the domination number is at most 4. title: Characterization of fixed ordering configurations by formal expansion fixedness
record_statement: Let $\mathcal{E}$ be a set of point labels and $\mathcal{B}$ a set of coordinate indices. A linear ordering configuration $\mathcal{C}$ on $(\mathcal{E},\mathcal{B})$ is **fixed** when the sign or non-nullity of $det(M_{\mathcal{E},\mathcal{B}})$ is determined by the prescribed coordinate orderings. It is **formally fixed by expansion** when some cofactor expansion of $det(M_{\mathcal{E},\mathcal{B}})$ with respect to a pair $(e_i,e_j)$ has formal sign $\fbox{+}$ or $\fbox{-}$, using the signs of the induced lower-dimensional determinants. **Expansion characterization conjecture.** The configuration $\mathcal{C}$ is fixed if and only if $\mathcal{C}$ is formally fixed by expansion. The implication from formal expansion fixedness to fixedness is established, but the converse is presented as a conjecture in the supplied text.

title: The two-round minimal percolating set conjecture
record_statement:
Let $\Pi_q$ be a finite projective plane of order $q$, let $r$ be the infection rate, and let $t_r(A)$ denote the percolation time of a percolating set $A$. **Two-round minimal percolating set conjecture.** For each $r$ with

$$
4\leq r\leq q,
$$

there exists a minimal percolating set $A_r$ with

$$
t_r(A_r)=2.
$$

title: The generalized parallel-loop sorting conjecture
record_statement:
Let $S\subseteq\mathbb{Z}$, and let $r(\mathbb{Z}\langle S\rangle)$ be obtained from $\mathbb{Z}\langle S\rangle$ by replacing every edge, including every loop, by $r$ parallel copies. Suppose $n\in\mathbb{N}$ satisfies

$$
\mathrm{min}(\widetilde{n\delta_0}^{\mathbb{Z}\langle S\rangle})<\mathrm{min}(\widetilde{(n-1)\delta_0}^{\mathbb{Z}\langle S\rangle})
$$

and

$$
\mathrm{max}(\widetilde{n\delta_0}^{\mathbb{Z}\langle S\rangle})>\mathrm{max}(\widetilde{(n-1)\delta_0}^{\mathbb{Z}\langle S\rangle}).
$$

**Generalized parallel-loop sorting conjecture.** Then $r(\mathbb{Z}\langle S\rangle)$ sorts $\Delta^{rn}$ for each $r\geq1$. This simultaneously generalizes the looped-path and parallel-edge conjectures, but the source supplies no proof of the general assertion.

title: The uniform central graph appendage conjecture for central graphs of diameter greater than one
record_statement:
Let $C$ and $P$ be graphs, let $\operatorname{diam}(C)$ and $\operatorname{diam}(P)$ denote their diameters, let $r(P)$ denote the radius of $P$, and let $A_{ucg}(C,P)$ be the corresponding appendage number. **The uniform central graph appendage conjecture.** If

$$
\operatorname{diam}(C)>1,
$$

and

$$
\operatorname{diam}(P)=4,\qquad r(P)=3,
$$

then

$$
A_{ucg}(C,P)=6.
$$

The preceding results show that in this case the appendage number is either $5$ or $6$; value $5$ would occur exactly when a certain covering number equals $2$, but no such example was found and impossibility was not proved.
source: Sul-Young Choi and Jonathan Needleman, “On Central-Peripheral Appendage Numbers of Uniform Central Graphs”, arXiv:1705.07982 (2017).
