title: The edge-pattern convex-combination conjecture
record_statement:
Let $P$ be a $d$-regular edge-rooted pattern of depth $r$ and girth $2r+2$. For each edge-rooted pattern, let $\mathbf{e}(P)$ denote its constraint vector, and let $\mathcal{T}'_r(d)$ be the specified family of $d$-regular edge-rooted trees of depth $r$. The constraint $\mathbf{e}(P)$ is **weaker** than a convex combination of constraints from this family in the sense that there exist $T_1,\dots,T_m\in\mathcal{T}'_r(d)$ and $\lambda_1,\dots,\lambda_m\in[0,1]$ with

$$
\sum_{i=1}^m\lambda_i=1
$$

and, for every $\bm{\alpha}\in{\left(\mathbb{Q}^+\right)}^{r+1}$,

$$
\bm{\alpha}^{\!\top}\left(\sum_{i=1}^m\lambda_i\mathbf{e}(T_i)\right)\ge 1\quad\implies\quad\bm{\alpha}^{\!\top}\mathbf{e}(P)\ge 1.
$$

This would explain why the bounds obtained from edge-rooted trees remain valid at girth $2r+2$, and would generalize the cases checked for $r=2$ and $d\in\{3,4\}$.
source: François Pirot and Jean-Sébastien Sereni, “Fractional chromatic number, maximum degree and girth”, arXiv:1904.05618 (2021).
row_statement: There is an eight-vertex cubic edge-rooted pattern in the source's sense, of exact depth two and girth six, whose constraint vector is not weaker than any finite convex combination of constraint vectors of acyclic cubic edge-rooted patterns of exact depth two. The positive rational vector (1/1000, 7/27, 1/3) gives a value below one on the pattern and above one on every tree constraint.
lean_vs_paper: Lean checks the pattern, exact-depth family classification, maximum independent-set expectations and separation for real convex weights. The written argument also covers the depth-at-most reading via the one shallower form.

title: The rainbow vertex-disconnection Nordhaus–Gaddum conjecture
record_statement:

$$

$$

title: Estrada–Mugnolo's Kirchhoff-index ordering conjecture for hubs-biased resistance distances
record_statement:
Let $G$ be a connected graph. Write $\mathcal{\mathcal{\mathscr{R}}_{\mathnormal{\alpha=1}}}(G)$ for the Kirchhoff index based on the hubs-repelling resistance distance, $\mathcal{\mathcal{\mathscr{R}}}_{\alpha=0}(G)$ for the standard Kirchhoff index, and $\mathcal{\mathcal{\mathscr{R}}_{\mathnormal{\alpha=-1}}}(G)$ for the Kirchhoff index based on the hubs-attracting resistance distance.

**Kirchhoff-index ordering conjecture.** For $\alpha\in\{-1,1\}$,

$$
\mathcal{\mathcal{\mathscr{R}}_{\mathnormal{\alpha=1}}}(G)\geq\mathcal{\mathcal{\mathscr{R}}}_{\alpha=0}(G)\geq\mathcal{\mathcal{\mathscr{R}}_{\mathnormal{\alpha=-1}}}(G),
$$

with equality if and only if $G$ is regular.

The conjecture was formulated after computational experiments on more than 12,000 connected graphs with $5\leq n\leq 8$, and predicts that hubs-repelling navigation gives the largest Kirchhoff index while hubs-attracting navigation gives the smallest. Its general validity is left open in the source.
source: Ernesto Estrada and Delio Mugnolo, “Hubs-biased resistance distances on graphs and networks”, arXiv:2101.07103 (2021).

title: Non-IR conjecture for paths and cycles
record_statement:

title: Subgraph criterion for minimal doubled 3-regular graphs
record_statement:
Let $G$ be a doubled 3-regular graph. Perform the YY-$\Delta$ transformation on all wyes in all possible ways to obtain a graph $G'$ of smallest size. A **chain of 3-cycles** is a chain of one or more 3-cycles, each connected by a vertex that is also doubly adjacent to one more vertex, with the 3-cycles at either end having one vertex with exactly 4 neighbours and no connections of size greater than 2.

title: The sparsity conjecture for minimally AP-irreducible sign pattern matrices
record_statement:
Let $A$ be a minimally AP-irreducible sign pattern matrix of order $n$ whose diagonal entries are all zero. A sign pattern matrix $A$ is **minimally AP-irreducible** if it is AP-irreducible and deleting any nonzero entry destroys AP-irreducibility. **Sparsity conjecture.** The matrix $A$ has at most $2n-2$ nonzero entries.

The paper establishes this bound under the additional hypothesis that $A[\alpha,\beta]$ contains no $+$ for any two distinct irreducible components $\alpha$ and $\beta$ of $A_+$. The conjecture asks whether the same bound holds without that additional hypothesis; its status is not resolved in the supplied text.
source: Sunil Das, “Sign patterns that allow algebraic positivity”, arXiv:2112.00442 (2022).

title: Unit-gap conjecture for diameters of Schrijver graphs
record_statement:
Let $k$ and $r$ be integers with $2\leq r\leq k-2$, and let $D(G)$ denote the diameter of a graph $G$. For $n=2k+r$, write $\operatorname{SG}(n,k)$ for the Schrijver graph. **Unit-gap conjecture.** If $2\leq r\leq k-2$, then

$$
D\left(\operatorname{SG}(2k+r,k)\right)-D\left(\operatorname{SG}(2k+r+1,k)\right)\in\\{0,1\\}.
$$

The conjecture concerns the possibility of larger drops in the diameter as $r$ increases. It is based on computations and is open; the paper notes that the analogous differences are in $\\{0,1\\}$ for $k\leq 5$, while a larger gap occurs at the transition from $r=1$ to $r=2$ when $k\geq 6$.

title: The exact $(k+1)$-metric dimension of three-dimensional grids
record_statement:
Let $k,n_1,n_2,n_3\ge 2$, and let $P_{n_1}\Box P_{n_2}\Box P_{n_3}$ be the three-dimensional grid graph. Write $\alpha_m(n_1,n_2,n_3)$ and $\alpha_M(n_1,n_2,n_3)$ for the quantities defined in the paper, and let $\dim_{k+1}$ denote the $(k+1)$-metric dimension.

**The conjecture.** If

$$
\alpha_m(n_1,n_2,n_3)\le k<\alpha_M(n_1,n_2,n_3),
$$

then

$$
\dim_{k+1}(P_{n_1}\Box P_{n_2}\Box P_{n_3})=\min\left\{4k-2\alpha_m(n_1,n_2,n_3)+4,\ n_1n_2n_3-(n_1-2)(n_2-2)(n_3-2)\right\}.
$$

The preceding results determine the exact value when $k<\alpha_m(n_1,n_2,n_3)$ and show that the displayed upper bound holds throughout the remaining range where a $(k+1)$-resolving set exists. The conjecture proposes the exact value in the intermediate range $\alpha_m(n_1,n_2,n_3)\le k<\alpha_M(n_1,n_2,n_3)$; when $\alpha_m=\alpha_M$, which occurs if $\min\{n_1,n_2,n_3\}=2$, the metric dimension is already completely determined.
source: Mercè Mora, María José Souto Salorio and Ana Dorotea Tarrío-Tobar, “Resolving sets tolerant to failures in three-dimensional grids”, arXiv:2112.08768 (2021).

title: Categorical genericity conjecture for the combinatorial derived matroid
record_statement:
Let $M$ be a representable matroid with set of circuits $\mathcal{C}$. For matroids on a fixed ground set, use the **weak order** defined by $M_1\geq M_2$ when every dependent set of $M_1$ is dependent in $M_2$. **Categorical genericity conjecture.** Then

$$
\delta M\geq\delta_{OW}(R)
$$

for every representation $R$ of $M$, where the order is the weak order on matroids with ground set $\mathcal{C}$. This claims that the combinatorial derived matroid is the generic, maximal derived matroid in the categorical weak-order sense.
source: Olga Kuznetsova, Ragnar Freij-Hollanti and Relinde Jurrius, “Combinatorial Derived Matroids”, arXiv:2206.06881 (2022).

title: The diagonal-monomial reachability conjecture for psd-stable polynomials
record_statement:
Let $f$ be a psd-stable polynomial in symmetric variables, and let $Z^\beta$ be a monomial appearing in a psd-stable polynomial. A **diagonal monomial** is a monomial $Z^\alpha$ appearing in $f$ whose variables are diagonal variables. The distance between monomials is measured by the norm used for exponent vectors, and linear, double, and transposition steps are the support-preserving monomial moves defined in the paper.

**Diagonal-monomial reachability conjecture.** For any monomial $Z^\beta$ appearing in a psd-stable polynomial, there is a diagonal monomial $Z^\alpha$ appearing in $f$ which can be reached by a sequence of linear, double and transposition steps which decrease the distance from $\beta$ to $\alpha$ and which never leave the support of $f$.

This conjecture proposes that the determinant's connectedness under support-preserving combinatorial moves extends to all psd-stable polynomials. Its resolution is not specified in the supplied text.
source: Giulia Codenotti, Stephan Gardoll and Thorsten Theobald, “Combinatorics and preservation of conically stable polynomials”, arXiv:2206.10913 (2022).
acceptance_record: not in ledger (round 2; pipeline complete; see packet)
row_statement: Conjecture 5.13 of Codenotti, Gardoll and Theobald (from every monomial in the support of a psd-stable polynomial a diagonal monomial of the support can be reached by linear, double and transposition steps that decrease the distance and stay in the support) is false when 'decrease' is strict, which is the source's usage: an explicit psd-stable cubic in the entries of a 3 x 3 symmetric matrix (a product of three forms u^T Z u) has a support monomial from which no diagonal monomial is reachable. Lean proves psd-stability over every complex symmetric matrix with positive definite imaginary part. Under non-strict decrease every monomial of this witness reaches a diagonal one, so that form is not refuted.

title: Improved upper bounds for Staller–Maker–Breaker domination numbers
record_statement:
Let $G$ be a graph on $n$ vertices, with minimum degree $\delta(G)$. The S-game and D-game parameters are denoted by $\gamma_{\rm SMB}'(G)$ and $\gamma_{\rm SMB}(G)$, respectively.

**Improved SMBD-number bounds.**

$$
\begin{aligned}
&\text{(i) If }\gamma_{\rm SMB}'(G)<\infty,\text{ then }\gamma_{\rm SMB}'(G)\le \left\lceil\frac{n}{2}\right\rceil-\delta(G)+1;\\
&\text{(ii) If }\gamma_{\rm SMB}(G)<\infty,\text{ then }\gamma_{\rm SMB}(G)\le \left\lfloor\frac{n}{2}\right\rfloor-\delta(G)+1.
\end{aligned}
$$

These bounds would improve the known sharp general upper bounds when the minimum degree is at least two; the authors note that sharp examples under this degree condition are not known.
source: Csilla Bujtás and Pakanun Dokyeesun, “Fast winning strategies for Staller in the Maker-Breaker domination game”, arXiv:2206.12812 (2022).
row_statement: A seven-vertex theta graph with branch lengths 2, 2 and 4 has minimum degree two and finite Staller-start winning number four, exceeding the proposed bound of three. Thus the conjunction of the Staller-start and Dominator-start bounds for finite winning numbers is false.
lean_vs_paper: Lean checks the exact Staller-start number, the budget-to-number bridge and the negation of both bounds taken together, also established in the paper by finite strategy analysis.

title: Strict middle-graph increase conjecture for outer-connected domination
record_statement:
Let $G$ be a graph of order $n\ge 2$. The **strict middle-graph increase conjecture** asserts that

$$
\gamma{\tilde{}} _{c}(G) < \gamma{\tilde{}} _{c}(M(G)).
$$

The paper notes that this inequality holds for trees and for several standard graph families, including complete graphs, wheels, friendship graphs, complete bipartite graphs, and cycles. Whether it holds for every graph of order at least two remains open.

title: Line-middle graph inequality conjecture for outer-connected domination
record_statement:
Let $G$ be a graph of order $n\ge 2$, and let $L(G)$ and $M(G)$ denote its line graph and middle graph, respectively. The **line-middle graph inequality conjecture** asserts that

$$
\gamma{\tilde{}} _{c}(L(G)) \le \gamma{\tilde{}} _{c}(M(G)).
$$

The inequality is supported by the preceding results, including strict inequality for wheels of order at least five; equality occurs for at least one connected graph of order four. A classification of graphs for which equality holds is posed separately as an open problem, while the general inequality remains open.
source: Farshad Kazemnejad, Behnaz Pahlavsay, Elisa Palezzato and Michele Torielli, “Connected and outer-connected domination number of middle graphs”, arXiv:2206.15439 (2022).

title: Hurlbert's ordering conjecture for universal cycles of permutations
record_statement: Let $S_n$ be the set of permutations of $[n]$, and let $\mathcal{O}(n)$ be the clustered graph of overlapping $n$-permutations: its edges are the permutations in $S_n$, and consecutive permutations overlap in their last and first $n-1$ entries up to reduction. **Hurlbert's ordering conjecture.** Given any Euler tour of the clustered graph of overlapping permutations (that is, an ordering of $S_n$ such that each consecutive pair of permutations overlaps), there is a universal cycle for permutations that covers $S_n$ in the same order. Universal cycles correspond to Euler tours in this graph, but it remains open whether every such ordering can be realized by a universal cycle.
source: Rachel Kirsch, Clare Sibley and Elizabeth Sprangel, “Graph Universal Cycles: Compression and Connections to Universal Cycles”, arXiv:2209.14198 (2022).
lean_endpoints: MathDB356266.conjecture_false : ¬ MathDB356266.Conjecture, where Conjecture := for all n N and every t : Fin (N+1) -> Fin (n+1) -> Fin (n+1) with EulerOrdering t (every row a permutation, rows distinct, every permutation occurring, every cyclic consecutive pair overlapping after reduction) there are K and a cyclic word w : Fin (N+1) -> Fin K whose windows realize t; also MathDB356266.conjectureLinear_false for words over an arbitrary linear order
row_statement: There is an Euler tour of the overlap graph on all permutations of four letters, using each permutation exactly once with matching reduced suffix and prefix at every cyclic transition, that no cyclic word realizes by its ordered windows. The impossibility holds over any linearly ordered alphabet.
lean_vs_paper: Lean checks the full overlap tour and its strict comparison cycle. The paper also translates the obstruction via the source correspondence to graph universal cycles and discusses classical related mechanisms.

title: Well-balanced orientation conjecture for maximum total arc-connectivity
record_statement: Let $G$ be a graph, let $\vec{G}$ be an orientation of $G$, and let $tac(\vec{G})$ denote its total arc-connectivity. An orientation **maximizes total arc-connectivity** when it maximizes $tac(\vec{G})$ among all orientations of $G$. **Well-balanced orientation conjecture.** Every graph $G$ has an orientation $\vec{G}$ that maximizes $tac(\vec{G})$ and is well-balanced. The source presents this as a stronger statement than the conjecture about 2-edge-connected graphs and does not give a resolution.
source: Florian Hörsch, “On orientations maximizing total arc-connectivity”, arXiv:2305.08688 (2023).

title: Linear-bound multiset reconstruction conjecture for tableau minors
record_statement: Let $k\geq 1$ and let $T\in\operatorname{YT}(n)$, where $n\geq k+4$. Here $\operatorname{mM}_k(T)$ denotes the multiset of $k$-minors of the standard Young tableau $T$. **Multiset reconstruction conjecture.** The multiset $\operatorname{mM}_k(T)$ determines $T$. This proposed linear bound is supported by computer verification for $k\leq 5$, and concerns reconstructibility from multisets of $k$-minors.
source: William Q. Erickson, Daniel Herden, Jonathan Meddaugh, Mark R. Sepanski, Cordell Hammon, Jasmin Mohn and Indalecio Ruiz-Bolanos, “Young tableau reconstruction via minors”, arXiv:2307.13161 (2023).

title: Conjecture that interval and integer Schur numbers coincide
record_statement:
Let $S(r)$ be the least positive integer $N$ such that every $r$-colouring of $[N]$ contains a monochromatic solution to $x+y=z$, and let $I(r)$ be the supremum of the real numbers $T>1$ for which the half-open interval $[1,T)$ admits a sum-free $r$-colouring. **Interval Schur number conjecture.** For all $r$, we have

$$
I(r)=S(r).
$$

The equality would make the bounds for $I(r)$ match up to logarithmic factors. The supplied text presents this as a belief and gives no resolution.
source: Lucas Aragão, Jonathan Chapman, Miquel Ortega and Victor Souza, “On the number of monochromatic solutions to multiplicative equations”, arXiv:2311.18742 (2024).

title: The set-palette conjecture for complete graphs
record_statement:
Let $K_n$ be the complete graph on $n$ vertices. In a general edge-coloring of $K_n$, let $\tau_s(n)$ denote the minimum number of colors needed so that all triangles have distinct color palettes when a palette is viewed as the set of colors appearing on its three edges. **Set-palette conjecture.** For $n\geq4$,

$$
\tau_s(n)=n-1.
$$

The source notes the inequality $\tau_m(n)\leq\tau_s(n)\leq\tau'(n)$ and states that this conjecture would imply the preceding multiset-palette conjecture. Its status is not resolved in the supplied text.
source: Monika Pilsniak and Mariusz Wozniak, “A note on edge colorings distinguishing all triangles in a graph”, arXiv:2407.19050 (2024).

title: Largest rigid facet conjecture for Vietoris–Rips complexes of hypercubes
record_statement:
Let $Q_n=\\{\pm1\\}^n$ be the Hamming cube with Hamming distance. A subset is **maximally diameter-$r$** if its diameter is $r$ and adjoining any point outside it produces diameter greater than $r$; it is **rigid** if every point has a point at distance equal to the diameter. Let $b'(n;r)$ be the size of the largest maximally diameter-$r$, rigid subset of $Q_n$, equivalently the largest such rigid facet in $\operatorname{\mathcal{VR}}(Q_n;r)$. **Largest rigid facet conjecture.**

$$
b'(n;r)=2^r
$$

whenever $n\geq r$. The subcube $Q_r\times\\{\mathbf 1_{n-r}\\}$ supplies an extremal candidate of size $2^r$, but the conjectured upper bound is not proved in the source.
source: Joseph Briggs, Ziqin Feng and Chris Wells, “Facets in the Vietoris–Rips complexes of hypercubes”, arXiv:2408.01288 (2024).
row_statement: In the signed eight-dimensional Hamming cube there is a 34-point subset of diameter exactly five, maximal under inclusion among sets of diameter at most five, with a distance-five partner for each point. Thus the greatest size of a rigid maximal diameter-r set need not be 2ʳ when r≤n.
lean_vs_paper: Lean verifies the subset in the Boolean encoding and transfers the refutation to the signed cube. The paper's independent exhaustive algorithm is supplementary.
adversarial_verdicts: NOT_COUNTED (adversarial-triage-E1-sol62-20261119-r1)
caveats: NOT_COUNTED applies to the submitted padded witness under the brief. The projected 34-point set and the independently found 33-point set are valid unpadded refutations at the smallest dimension.
The underlying seven-dimensional counterexample was not found in the two public archives.

title: The local antimagic chromatic number conjecture for joins of matching and null graphs
record_statement:
Let $r,s\ge 1$ and $m\ge 2$. For a graph $G$, its **local antimagic chromatic number** $\chi_{la}(G)$ is the least number of distinct induced vertex labels among bijective local antimagic edge labelings of $G$. Let $(2s+1)P_2$ be the disjoint union of $2s+1$ copies of the two-vertex path, let $O_m$ be the null graph on $m$ vertices, let $\vee$ denote the graph join, and let $2r((2s+1)P_2\vee O_m)$ be the disjoint union of $2r$ copies of this join.

**Local antimagic chromatic number conjecture.**

$$
\chi_{la}\bigl(2r((2s+1)P_2\vee O_m)\bigr)=3.
$$

This is posed as an open problem in the conclusion, extending results on local antimagic chromatic numbers for joins of special graph families. The claim predicts a constant value of $3$ throughout the stated parameter range.
source: Gee-Choon Lau and Wai Chee Shiu, “On local antimagic chromatic number of the join of two special families of graphs – II”, arXiv:2410.17674 (2024).
lean_endpoints: not_conjecture41 : ¬ Conjecture41, where Conjecture41 := ∀ r s m : ℕ, 1 ≤ r → 1 ≤ s → 2 ≤ m → Antimagic.chiLA (LauShiu.graph r s m) = 3; LauShiu.graph r s m is the SimpleGraph 2r((2s+1)P_2 join O_m) and chiLA is the least colour count of local antimagic labellings (edge bijections onto 1..|E| with distinct weights on adjacent vertices), the definitions reused byte-identically from the accepted 354228 packet
row_statement: It is false that for every integer r,s ≥ 1 and m ≥ 2 the disjoint union of 2r copies of the join of (2s+1) disjoint edges with an independent m-set has local antimagic chromatic number three. At r=s=1,m=2 there is no bijective edge labelling by 1 through the edge count with distinct sums across adjacent vertices and at most three distinct vertex sums.

title: Treewidth-connectivity partition conjecture for graphs
record_statement: Let $G$ be a graph, and let $k$ be an integer such that $G$ has treewidth at most $k$ and connectivity at least $k$. A vertex set inducing a graph of treewidth at most $k-1$ and connectivity at least $k-1$ is denoted by $\mathcal{T}$, and an independent set is denoted by $\mathcal{I}$. **Treewidth-connectivity partition conjecture.** The vertices of $G$ can be partitioned into an induced graph $\mathcal{T}$ of treewidth at most $k-1$ and connectivity at least $k-1$, and an independent set $\mathcal{I}$. This is proposed as a generalization of a theorem for graphs of treewidth at most $2$; the source leaves it as a belief rather than an established result.
source: Stijn Cambie, François Dross, Kolja Knauer, Hoang La and Petru Valicov, “Partitions of planar (oriented) graphs into a connected acyclic and an independent set”, arXiv:2412.11774 (2025).

title: The majorization characterization conjecture for ordinal spaces embeddable in the line
record_statement:
Let $(X,\delta)$ be an ordinal space with $|X|=n\in\mathbb N^+$, and let $x_1,x_2,\ldots,x_n$ be an enumeration of its points satisfying the majorization property. Write $X\hookrightarrow\mathbb R^1$ for embeddability of $X$ in the real line. **Majorization characterization conjecture.** If such an enumeration exists, then

$$
X\hookrightarrow\mathbb R^1.
$$

The paper proves that line embeddability implies the existence of an enumeration with the majorization property and states sufficiency for $n\leqslant4$, while explicitly saying that it cannot determine whether sufficiency holds for $n>5$; the general assertion is therefore open.
source: Karsten Keller and Evgeniy Petrov, “Ordinal spaces”, arXiv:2412.17391 (2024).
row_statement: There is a six-point ordinal space with no ties between distinct off-diagonal pairs whose displayed enumeration has the majorization property for nondecreasing chains of every positive length, including repeats and permutations of the successive pieces, but which does not embed into the real line preserving distance comparisons. Thus the majorization property of an enumeration does not imply line embeddability.
lean_vs_paper: Lean checks the reductions to finitely many chains and the comparison obstruction, as in the paper. The paper also shows equivalence of the two readings of the strict chain comparison and gives an ordinary linear-feasibility interpretation.
adversarial_verdicts: SEARCH_EASY (adversarial-triage-E1-sol62-20261119-r1)
caveats: 2020 journal body was unavailable to the recorded prior sweep. Scope and numbering follow arXiv v1, §7.

title: Positive matching decomposition conjecture for Cartesian products of cycles

$$
\mathrm{pmd}(C_m\square C_n)=6
$$

for all $m,n\geq3$ such that $m+n$ is even, or such that $(m,n)\in\{(3,4),(3,6),(5,6)\}$. The supplied text presents this exact-value assertion after an analysis of positive matchings in the relevant Cartesian products; no resolution beyond that analysis is provided.

record_statement: Let $\Omega(P;t)$ denote the order polynomial of a finite poset $P$. The classes under consideration are posets of width two, cell posets of cylindric skew shapes, and cell posets of shifted skew shapes; these classes are closed under taking lower and upper ideals. **Positivity conjecture.** The order polynomials of all three classes have nonnegative coefficients: posets of width two, cell posets of cylindric skew shapes, and cell posets of shifted skew shapes. title: Automorphism count from companion multiplicities
record_statement:
Let $P$ be a poset with $n$ elements, and let $\mathcal{A}_1,\ldots,\mathcal{A}_k$ be the mutually different collections of type $\mathrm{Comp}(P,\omega)$ for $\omega\in\Sigma_P$. Suppose that $\mathcal{A}_i$ appears for $l_i$ different $P$-listings, so that $l_1+\cdots+l_k=n!$. Let $A(P)$ denote the number of automorphisms of $P$. **Automorphism-count conjecture.** For any poset $P$,

$$
A(P)=\mathrm{min}\{l_i\}.
$$

The preceding discussion establishes the lower bound $A(P)\leq l_i$ for every $i$ and proposes that the smallest companion multiplicity exactly recovers the automorphism count; no resolution is supplied in the excerpt.
source: Stefan Mitrovic, “Linear function of a poset”, arXiv:2504.20975 (2025).

title: Propagation-time interval conjecture for minimum zero forcing sets of hypercubes
record_statement:
Let $Q_d$ be the $d$-dimensional hypercube graph. A **minimum zero forcing set** is a zero forcing set of cardinality equal to the zero forcing number of $Q_d$; its propagation time is the number of parallel forcing rounds needed to color all vertices. Let $\operatorname{pt}(Q_d)$ and $\operatorname{PT}(Q_d)$ denote the minimum and maximum propagation times, respectively, among minimum zero forcing sets of $Q_d$. A graph has a **full propagation time interval** if it has minimum zero forcing sets with every integer propagation time between $\operatorname{pt}(Q_d)$ and $\operatorname{PT}(Q_d)$. 

**Propagation-time interval conjecture.** For every $d\geq 2$, 

$$
\operatorname{pt}(Q_d)=1 \quad\text{and}\quad \operatorname{PT}(Q_d)=2^{d-2}.
$$

Moreover, $Q_d$ has a full propagation time interval.

The preceding results establish the existence of minimum zero forcing sets with propagation times $1$, $2$, $3$, and $4$ for $d\geq 4$, and hence already give non-automorphic minimum zero forcing sets. The conjecture predicts the complete range of propagation times through the claimed maximum $2^{d-2}$; the source states that this remains open, together with the enumeration of all minimum zero forcing sets of $Q_d$.
source: Boris Brimkov, Thomas R. Cameron and Owen Grubbs, “On the forts and related parameters of the hypercube graph”, arXiv:2507.10826 (2025).

title: The edge-redundant rigidity conjecture for complete graphs in $\ell_\infty^d$
record_statement:
Let $d\geq 2$, let $n\geq 2d+2$, and let $K_n$ denote the complete graph on $n$ vertices. A graph is **edge-redundantly rigid** in a normed space if it has a framework that is infinitesimally rigid and remains infinitesimally rigid after deleting any edge. **Edge-redundant rigidity conjecture.** For every $d\geq 2$ and every $n\geq 2d+2$, the complete graph $K_n$ is edge-redundantly rigid in $\ell_\infty^d$.

The preceding proposition rules out $K_{2d+1}$, so the conjecture asserts that the stated threshold is sufficient as well as necessary. The supplied excerpt gives no evidence that the conjecture has been resolved.
source: James Cruickshank, Sean Dewar and Derek Kitson, “Algebraic connectivity in normed spaces”, arXiv:2508.00134 (2025).
row_statement: No well-positioned framework of K₈ in ℓ∞³ is infinitesimally rigid and stays so after every single-edge deletion. This refutes the universal threshold n≥2d+2 at d=3,n=8, while an explicit well-positioned framework of K₉ in ℓ∞³ does have that property.
lean_vs_paper: Lean checks the original normed-space rigidity definitions, geometric and combinatorial bridges, unsatisfiability via a verified checker, and K₉. The positive extension to n≥10 and the resulting exact complete-graph threshold in dimension three are established in the paper.

caveats: This is a universal nonexistence result about well-positioned placements of K8, with a separate positive K9 result. The counting judgment rests on fast systematic exhaustion at the first open size, with exact verification of all 827 obstructions.

The accepted proof uses seven forbidden patterns and a kernel-checked SAT certificate. This independent triage uses signed edge enumeration and exact rational linear-infeasibility certificates. The accepted positive extension for n≥10 is paper-only.

title: Gatzweiler–Krattenthaler conjecture on positivity of Stanton fractions
record_statement:
Let $m,n$ be positive integers with $m\geq n$, let $\mathbf{a}=(a_1,\ldots,a_n)$ be a sequence of non-negative integers, and consider

$$
\frac{\prod_{i=1}^n(1-q^{m+i})^{a_i}}{\prod_{i=1}^n(1-q^i)^{a_i}}.
$$

**Gatzweiler–Krattenthaler conjecture.** If this fraction is a polynomial in $q$, then it has non-negative coefficients. This is presented as a strengthening of Stanton's conjecture, removing both the assumed polynomiality for every non-negative $m$ and the symmetry condition on $\mathbf{a}$. The supplied text does not report a proof or disproof of this strengthened claim.
source: Mona Gatzweiler, Fabián Levicán-Santibáñez and Atsuro Yoshida, “Cyclotomic generating functions, empty weighted complete intersections and positivity”, arXiv:2603.22226 (2026).

title: Conjecture on non-full-weight cyclic codes over \(\mathbb F_3\)
record_statement:
Let $n>3$ be a prime, and let $\operatorname{ord}_n(3)$ denote the multiplicative order of $3$ modulo $n$. Set

$$
r=\frac{n-1}{\operatorname{ord}_n(3)}.
$$

Let $\mathcal N(n,3)$ denote the family of cyclic codes over $\mathbb F_3$ containing no full-weight codeword. **The cyclic-code counting conjecture.** If $\operatorname{ord}_n(3)$ is odd, then

$$
|\mathcal N(n,3)|=\sum_{j=0}^{\frac r2}\binom{r}{j}.
$$

The formula refines a lower bound for $|\mathcal N(n,3)|$; the case $n=13$ gives $11$ cyclic codes, while the conjecture remains unproved in the stated generality.
source: Yangcheng Li and Pingzhi Yuan, “Cyclic Codes and Cyclically Covering Subspaces over Finite Fields”, arXiv:2607.02239 (2026).
acceptance_record: not in ledger (round 2; pipeline complete; see packet)
row_statement: Conjecture 4.1 of Li and Yuan (for a prime n > 3 with ord_n(3) odd and r = (n-1)/ord_n(3), the number of cyclic codes over F_3 of length n with no full-weight codeword equals the sum of binom(r,j) for 0 <= j <= r/2) is false at n = 109, where ord_109(3) = 27 and r = 4: the family of shift-invariant subspaces of F_3^109 with no all-nonzero vector has at most 9 members, while the formula gives 11. title: Hamiltonian-path distance congruence conjecture for Cartesian products of directed cycles
record_statement:
Let $X$ be the Cartesian product of $k$ directed cycles of lengths $m_1,m_2,\ldots,m_k$, where $k\geq 3$ and each $m_i\geq 2$. For vertices $u$ and $v$ of $X$, let $d_X(u,v)$ denote the length of a shortest directed path from $u$ to $v$. **Hamiltonian-path distance congruence conjecture.** There is a Hamiltonian path from $u$ to $v$ if and only if

$$
d_X(u,v)\equiv -1\pmod{\gcd(m_1,m_2,\ldots,m_k)}.
$$
 This generalizes the coprime-length case, in which the congruence condition is automatic, and remains open according to the supplied source.
source: David Austin, Heather Gavlas and Dave Witte, “Hamiltonian Paths in Cartesian Powers of Directed Cycles”, arXiv:math/0110073 (2001).
row_statement: In the Cartesian product of directed cycles of lengths (2,2,3), the distinct vertices u=(0,0,0) and v=(0,0,1) have shortest directed distance 1, and the distance is −1 modulo the gcd 1, but there is no directed Hamiltonian path from u to v. Hence the universal equivalence fails both for arbitrary endpoints and for distinct endpoints.
lean_vs_paper: Lean checks the minimum directed distance and exact finite path nonexistence, using a kernel-reduced subset recurrence. The paper also gives a structural proof by column intervals and modular advance counts.

title: The layered extremal word conjecture
record_statement:
Let $\Pi$ be a set of layered patterns, and let $\delta(\Pi)$ denote their packing density and $\delta'(\Pi)$ the corresponding density when the alphabet size is fixed as in the paper. A string is **layered** if it is formed from layers, and a maximal $\Pi$-containing string is one attaining the maximum number of occurrences of patterns in $\Pi$.

**Layered extremal word conjecture.** If $\Pi$ is a set of layered patterns, then

$$
\delta'(\Pi)=\delta(\Pi),
$$

and among maximal $\Pi$-containing strings in $[k]^n$, there is one which is layered.

This conjecture asserts that restricting to layered strings does not reduce the packing density for sets of layered patterns, and that a layered extremal string always exists. The supplied context does not establish the claim or give a resolution status.
source: A. Burstein, Peter Hästö and T. Mansour, “Packing patterns into words”, arXiv:math/0212343 (2003).
outcome: REFUTED (layered-maximiser clause; the density equality is true)

29.

title: The growth constant for the stack-sorting map
record_statement:
Let $S_n$ be the symmetric group, let $s:S_n\to S_n$ be the stack-sorting map, and let $\deg(s:S_n\to S_n)$ denote its maximum fiber size. The paper considers the exponential growth rate

$$
\lim\limits_{n\to\infty}\deg(s:S_n\to S_n)^{1/n}.
$$

**Stack-sorting growth conjecture.** The value of this limit lies in the interval $(1.68,1.73)$.

The interval is suggested by computations on random permutations for $n=100$ and $n=300$. The problem of obtaining improved asymptotic estimates, or exact formulas, remains open.
source: Colin Defant and James Propp, “Quantifying Noninvertibility in Discrete Dynamical Systems”, arXiv:2002.07144 (2020).

row_statement: The nth roots of the average West stack-sorting fibre multiplicity on Sₙ, given by the number of ordered pairs with equal image divided by n!, have no real limit in (1.68, 1.73), and exceed 1.73 arbitrarily late. title: Linear-growth conjecture for Split Smallest and Combine Smallest games
record_statement:
A Zeckendorf game starts from the Zeckendorf decomposition of $n$ and proceeds by legal combining and splitting moves; the **Split Smallest** and **Combine Smallest** games are deterministic strategies, and the number of moves is measured as the total number of moves in the resulting game.

title: The outerplane adjacency-polytope volume formula
record_statement:
Let $G$ be an outerplane graph. For each connected component $G_i$ of $G$, let $B_{i,1},\dots,B_{i,b_i}$ be its blocks; let $\mathscr{F}(B_{i,j})$ denote the bounded faces of $B_{i,j}$, let $\operatorname{ewd}{B_{i,j}}$ denote its extended weak dual, and let $v_F$ be the vertex of this dual corresponding to $F$. The normalized volume of the type-PQ adjacency polytope is denoted by $\operatorname{NVol}(\nabla^{\operatorname{PQ}}_G)$. **Outerplane adjacency-polytope volume conjecture.** For any outerplane graph $G$,

$$
\operatorname{NVol}(\nabla^{\operatorname{PQ}}_G) = \prod_{i=1}^k \prod_{j=1}^{b_i} 2^{|V(B_{i,j})| - 2|\mathscr{F}(B_{i,j})|}\prod_{F \in \mathscr{F}(B_{i,j})} \deg_{\operatorname{ewd}{B_{i,j}}}(v_F).
$$

The formula is proved for a proper but large class of outerplane graphs, namely those whose bounded faces are adjacent to the outer face, while experimental data suggests that it holds for all outerplane graphs; a proof remains open.
source: Robert Davis and Tianran Chen, “Computing Volumes of Adjacency Polytopes via Draconian Sequences”, arXiv:2007.11051 (2022).
row_statement: SOURCE-SCOPE RESULT: the formula proved is the one printed in the source (Davis–Chen Eq. (9), exponent 1 + Σ(|F| − 3) per block), not the one in the MathDB record, which mis-transcribes the exponent as |V| − 2|F| and is already false for K₂ and for the square with a chord. With that reading, and with an isolated-vertex block contributing 1 (the printed Eq. (9) and the source's own proved Corollary 35 give 2 there, where the volume is 1), the conjecture holds for every outerplane graph. The new step is an ear formula: removing a minimal ear of a polygon dissection multiplies the number of draconian sequences by an explicit factor with a defect term, and the defect vanishes because the attachment edge is an outer edge of what remains; induction gives the count 2^{1+S}·∏ deg for every polygon dissection, including dissections with inner faces that the source's recurrences (its Theorem 34 and Corollary 35) and Davis–Jakovleski–Pan's triangle recurrence do not reach. Lean proves the draconian count for every polygon dissection on n ≥ 3 vertices. The passage to normalized volumes of all outerplane graphs is on paper: the source's Theorem 8 (via Postnikov), Proposition 12, the leaf-block case of Theorem 13, and the identification of 2-connected outerplane graphs with polygon dissections.

title: Symmetry classification conjecture for board isomorphisms
record_statement:
Let $\mathcal{D}$ be the set of eight arrow directions, let $\operatorname{Mat}_{n\times n}(\mathcal{D})$ be the set of boards, and let $\operatorname{Sym}(\operatorname{Mat}_{n\times n}(\mathcal{D}))$ be the group of coordinate permutations and direction permutations that preserve graph isomorphism for every board. Let $R$ be reflection through the main diagonal, defined by $R(A)_{ij}=(a_{ji})^T$. **Symmetry classification conjecture.**

$$
\operatorname{Sym}(\operatorname{Mat}_{n\times n}(\mathcal{D}))=\{Id,R\}.
$$

The reflection $R$ is known to belong to this symmetry group, so the assertion is that it is the only nontrivial universal symmetry of boards. The source provides no resolution of this classification question.
source: Ary Shaviv, “Board games, random boards and long boards”, arXiv:2110.05416 (2021).
row_statement: For every odd n≥3, give each n×n compass board the directed graph of all positive ray steps from each cell, with the upper-left and center vertices fixed as named roots. Among maps induced by a cell permutation and one global permutation of the eight directions, exactly identity and physical main-diagonal reflection preserve rooted digraph isomorphism for every board, with the isomorphism allowed to depend on the board.

title: The equivalence of NT-balanced and ultra NT-balanced graphs
record_statement:
Let $G$ be a graph. For vertices $u,v$ and an integer $a$, let $n_a(u,v)$ be the number of vertices whose distance difference relative to $u$ and $v$ equals $a$. Call $G$ **NT-balanced** when $n_a(u,v)=n_a(v,u)$ for every pair of vertices $u,v$ and every relevant integer $a$. Call it **ultra NT-balanced** when, for every pair $u,v$, there is an involution of the vertex set pairing vertices counted by $n_a(u,v)$ with vertices counted by $n_a(v,u)$.

**NT-balance equivalence conjecture.** Every NT-balanced graph is also ultra NT-balanced.

The paper proves that ultra NT-balanced graphs are closed under Cartesian products and uses this to construct arbitrarily large examples. Whether every NT-balanced graph admits the required involutions remains open.
source: Linus Tang, “Extremal Bounds on Peripherality Measures”, arXiv:2306.15702 (2023).

title: The achromatic number bound by the harmonic index
record_statement:
Let $G$ be a graph. The **achromatic number** $psi(G)$ is the largest number of colors in a complete proper vertex coloring, and $R'(G)$ denotes the inverse degree-based index used in the source. **The achromatic-number conjecture.**

$$
\psi(G)\leq 2R'(G).
$$

The source presents this as a conjecture motivated by the preceding bounds. Its status is not resolved in the supplied text.
source: Baoyindureng Wu and Clive Elphick, “Upper bounds for the achromatic and coloring numbers of a graph”, arXiv:1511.00537 (2015).
row_statement: PROVED for graphs with an edge (Wu-Elphick 2015, Conjecture 4.1): for every finite simple graph G with at least one edge, psi(G) <= 2R'(G), where R'(G) = sum over edges uv of 1/max{d(u), d(v)}. More strongly, every complete colouring (proper or not) uses at most 2R'(G) colours, so the pseudoachromatic and Grundy numbers obey the same bound (Conjecture 4.2). The literal 'for any graph' fails exactly on nonempty edgeless graphs (psi = 1, R' = 0). These are the only exceptions, and Lean proves this exact truth set.

caveats: Proved for every graph with at least one edge. The literal 'for any graph' is false only on nonempty edgeless graphs (psi = 1 > 0 = 2R'), which the source's conventions implicitly exclude. Do not write 'for any graph'.
The MathDB title says 'harmonic index', but its statement uses R' (the modified Randic index). Since R' <= H, the harmonic-index reading also follows.
Significance modest: a short elementary counting proof, not a deep result.

title: The finite-cycle character-value coincidence conjecture for symmetric groups
record_statement:
Let $X$ be a finite set of permutations, and let $k\geq 1$ be an integer. For a permutation $g\in S_n$, its cycle type is the multiset of lengths of its cycles.

title: The star characterization conjecture for graphs with one large Laplacian eigenvalue
record_statement: Let $G$ be a finite simple graph with Laplacian eigenvalues $\mu_1\geq\cdots\geq\mu_n$ and average degree $\overline{d}(G)=2m/n$, where $m$ is the number of edges and $n$ the number of vertices. Define $\sigma(G)$ to be the number of Laplacian eigenvalues at least $\overline{d}(G)$. For integers $r\geq 1$ and $s\geq 0$, let $K_{1,r}+sK_1$ denote the disjoint union of the star $K_{1,r}$ and $s$ isolated vertices. **Star characterization conjecture.** $\sigma(G)=1$ if and only if $G$ is isomorphic to $K_1$, $K_2+sK_1$ for some $s\geq 0$, or $K_{1,r}+sK_1$ for some $r\geq 2$ and $0\leq s<r-1$. The conjecture seeks a complete structural characterization of graphs having exactly one Laplacian eigenvalue at least their average degree; the paper proves it for several classes, including graphs whose complements are disconnected, but the general case remains open.
source: L. Emilio Allem, Antonio Cafure, Ezequiel Dratman, Luciano N. Grippo, Martín D. Safe and Vilmar Trevisan, “Partial characterization of graphs having a single large Laplacian eigenvalue”, arXiv:1710.01710 (2017).
row_statement: A graph on n >= 1 vertices has exactly one Laplacian eigenvalue greater than or equal to its average degree (sigma(G) = 1, eigenvalues counted with multiplicity) if and only if n = 1, or G is K_{1,1} with any number s of isolated vertices, or G is a star K_{1,r} with r >= 2 together with s < r - 1 isolated vertices. No connectivity is assumed; for connected graphs this says that the stars are the only graphs with sigma = 1, the conjecture of Allem, Cafure, Dratman, Grippo, Safe and Trevisan, who proved it for forests, cographs, split graphs and other classes. The proof uses the bound mu_2 >= d_2 to reduce to connected graphs with a single vertex above the average degree, takes a Schur complement at that vertex, and closes the case by a degree-deficit count. Mathlib has no Courant-Fischer theorem, so Lean builds the link between counting eigenvalues above a threshold and subspaces on which the quadratic form is large, and proves the bound on the second largest Laplacian eigenvalue.

title: Asymptotic independence of descent sets and being an n-cycle
record_statement:
For each $n$, let $[n-1]=\{1,\ldots,n-1\}$, and let $\beta_n(I)$ denote the number of permutations in $S_n$ with descent set $I\subseteq[n-1]$, while $\beta^{\mathrm{cyc}}_n(I)$ denotes the number of $n$-cycles with descent set $I$. **Asymptotic independence conjecture.**

$$
\lim_{n\to\infty}\max_{\varnothing \subsetneqq I \subsetneqq [n-1]} \left| \frac{n\, \beta^{\mathrm{cyc}}_n(I)}{\beta_n(I)} - 1\right| = 0.
$$

This asserts that, uniformly over all non-empty proper descent sets, having descent set $I$ and being an $n$-cycle are asymptotically independent, with the proportion of $n$-cycles tending to $1/n$ as it does among all permutations. The source presents this as a conjectural strengthening of the known asymptotic independence result for alternating permutations.
source: Sergi Elizalde and Justin M. Troyka, “Exact and asymptotic enumeration of cyclic permutations according to descent set”, arXiv:1710.05103 (2019).
row_statement: The conjecture holds. The source's own Theorem 3.1(c) writes n·β^cyc_n(I) as β_n(I) plus a signed sum, over the divisors d ≥ 2 of n, of the counts β_{n/d}(I/d) for the compressed descent sets, so everything reduces to showing that these smaller counts are negligible against β_n(I) uniformly in I. The source's bound for them is absolute and fails when β_n(I) is small. The new step is a counting inequality, β_n(I) ≥ (n^{2/3}/40)·β_{n/d}(I/d) for every divisor d ≥ 2 and every nonempty proper I: each permutation counted on the right is inflated into blocks and then modified either by swaps of disjoint free pairs (decoded by block rank sums) or by sliding a single letter along a long monotone run (at most four preimages), giving many distinct permutations with descent set I. With τ(n) ≤ 2√n this gives |n·β^cyc_n(I)/β_n(I) − 1| ≤ 80·n^{−1/6}. Lean defines β and β^cyc literally (permutations with exact descent set in one-line notation; cycles with full support), proves the counting inequality, the bound and the printed limit of the maximum, and takes Theorem 3.1(c) of the source as an explicit hypothesis.

title: Odd-coordinate kernel conjecture for singular io-decomposable Riordan graphs
record_statement:
Let $G_n(g,zg)$ be a singular io-decomposable Riordan graph, let ${\cal A}_n$ be its adjacency matrix, and let $X=[x_1,x_2,\ldots,x_n]^T$ be an eigenvector with eigenvalue $0$. Define the odd-index and even-index subvectors by

$$
X_o=[x_1,x_3,\ldots,x_{2\lceil n/2\rceil-1}]^T,
$$

$$
X_e=[x_2,x_4,\ldots,x_{2\lfloor n/2\rfloor}]^T.
$$

**Odd-coordinate kernel conjecture.** Then

$$
X_o=O_{\lceil n/2\rceil}.
$$

This claim is motivated by Sage computations and, together with the preceding block-matrix lemma, would constrain the zero-eigenspace of every singular io-decomposable Riordan graph. No proof or resolution is supplied.

title: Submodular separation conjecture for low-degree monomial families
record_statement:
Let $0\leqslant r\leqslant d$ be integers and let $n=\binom{d}{\leqslant r}$. Define

$$
\phi:\{0,1\}^d\to\{0,1\}^n,
\qquad \phi(x)=\left(\prod_{i\in S}x_i\right)_{S\subset[d]:|S|\leqslant r},
$$

and let ${\mathcal F}_{r,d}=\phi(\{0,1\}^d)$. A function $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\mathbb Z$ is **submodular** if $f(x)+f(y)\geqslant f(x\vee y)+f(x\wedge y)$ for all $x,y$.

**Submodular separation conjecture.** For every such $r,d$, there exists a submodular function $f$ such that $f(x)$ is computable in $\mathrm{poly}(n)$ time, $f(x)\leqslant-1$ for every $x\in\mathcal F_{r,d}$, and $f(x)\geqslant0$ for every $x\notin\mathcal F_{r,d}$. If true, this would yield a hardness result for submodular minimization with modular constraints, complementing the known prime-power algorithms; the source does not resolve the conjecture.
source: Joshua Brakensiek, Sivakanth Gopi and Venkatesan Guruswami, “CSPs with Global Modular Constraints: Algorithms and Hardness via Polynomial Representations”, arXiv:1902.04740 (2019).

title: Equitable partitions of rectangular grid graphs
record_statement:
Let $P_m\oblong P_n$ be the rectangular grid graph, and let its automorphism group act naturally on its vertices. An equitable partition is a partition in which every vertex in a cell has the same number of neighbors in each cell.

**Grid-graph equitable-partition conjecture.** The equitable partitions of $P_m\oblong P_n$ are the orbit partitions of natural actions of the subgroups of the automorphism group of the graph. The lattice of equitable partitions is isomorphic to the lattice of subgroups exactly when there is a vertex with trivial stabilizer subgroup. This happens unless $2\le m=n\le3$.

title: Latin-strategy characterization conjecture for the symmetric group
record_statement:
Let $\mathbb{S}_n$ be the symmetric group on $n$ elements. A **Latin strategy** is obtained by choosing an $n\times n$ Latin square $S$; Alice's message identifies a row of $S$ that agrees with the input permutation at the maximum possible number of positions. title: Signed cycle-type restriction polynomiality conjecture
record_statement:
Let $n$ be a positive integer, let $k$ be a fixed positive integer with $1\leq k\leq n$, and let $\mathfrak{S}_n$ denote the symmetric group on $n$ elements. For $\pi\in\mathfrak{S}_n$, let $\operatorname{type}(\pi)$ be its cycle type, and let $\operatorname{RLMv}(\pi)$ and $\operatorname{EXCv}(\pi)$ denote its right-to-left-minimum-value and excedance-value multisets, respectively. Then **the polynomiality conjecture.**

$$
\sum_{\substack{\pi\in\mathfrak{S}_n\\min(\operatorname{type}(\pi))\geq k}}(-1)^{\operatorname{inv}(\pi)}\mathbf{x}_{\operatorname{RLMv}(\pi)}\mathbf{y}_{\operatorname{EXCv}(\pi)}
$$

is an element of $\mathbb{N}[x_1,\dotsc,x_n,y_1,\dotsc,y_n]$. This generalizes the derangement case by imposing a lower bound on the lengths of all cycles; the source provides no resolution or further evidence for the claim, so its status remains open.

title: The Polynexus formula for nonzero products in the rook monoid
record_statement:
Let $M_n$ be the monoid of rook diagrams and let $\mathbf{0}$ denote its zero element. Let $\psi(n)$ be the number of nonzero products arising from $M_n\setminus\{\mathbf{0}\}$.

**Polynexus conjecture.** For $n\in\mathbb{N}$, $\psi(n)$ equals the $(n+1)$th Polynexus number of order $7$, namely

$$
\psi(n)=\frac{(n+1)^7-n^7-(n+1)^3+n^3}{120}.
$$

The formula was suggested by numerical evaluation of the sextuple sum defining $\psi(n)$ and comparison with the Polynexus numbers. An analytic evaluation of that sum was not available in the source, so the conjecture remains open here.

title: Balanced-graph conjecture for flat graphs
record_statement:
Let $G$ be a flat graph, and let $c_i(G)$ denote the number of $i$-cliques in $G$. Define

$$

title: Congruence conjectures for permanents of shifted difference matrices
record_statement:
For a positive integer $n$, let $[j-k+\delta_{jk}]_{1\leqslant j,k\leqslant n}$ denote the $n\times n$ matrix whose $(j,k)$ entry is $j-k+\delta_{jk}$, where $\delta_{jk}$ is the Kronecker delta, and let $\operatorname{per}(M)$ denote the permanent of a matrix $M$. **Congruence conjecture.** For any prime $p$,

$$
\operatorname{per}[j-k+\delta_{jk}]_{1\leqslant j,k\leqslant p-1}\equiv 3\pmod p.
$$

For any odd prime $p$,

$$
\operatorname{per}[j-k+\delta_{jk}]_{1\leqslant j,k\leqslant p}\equiv 1+4p\pmod {p^2}.
$$

These assertions are motivated by the preceding determinant evaluation in the paper; no resolution or external evidence concerning either congruence is supplied here.
source: Han Wang and Zhi-Wei Sun, “Evaluations of some Toeplitz-type determinants”, arXiv:2206.12317 (2023).
row_statement: For B_n=(j−k+δ_jk) with 1≤j,k≤n, every prime p satisfies per(B_{p−1})≡3 modulo p. Every odd prime p satisfies per(B_p)≡1+4p modulo p².
lean_vs_paper: Lean checks both congruences for the actual Mathlib permanent. The written proof uses a different choice of finite-field multiplier in one intermediate argument.

title: Yip's maximal subfield clique conjecture for generalized Paley graphs
record_statement: Let $d>1$ be an integer. Let $q \equiv 1 \pmod {2d}$ be a power of a prime $p$, and let $r$ be the largest integer such that $d \mid \frac{q-1}{p^r-1}$. The subfield $\mathbb{F}_{p^r}$ is a clique in the generalized Paley graph $GP(q,d)=\operatorname{Cay}(\mathbb{F}_q^+;(\mathbb{F}_q^*)^d)$. **Yip's maximal subfield clique conjecture.** The subfield $\mathbb{F}_{p^r}$ forms a maximal clique in $GP(q,d)$. This conjecture asserts that the largest subfield producing a subfield clique cannot be extended to a larger clique. The paper resolves it in a stronger form under a sufficient-size hypothesis, while the unrestricted statement is the conjecture being addressed.
source: Chi Hoi Yip, “Maximality of subfields as cliques in Cayley graphs over finite fields”, arXiv:2209.00864 (2022).
row_statement: In every field of order 5⁸, the largest eligible subfield for d=3 is the prime field of order five, and it is properly contained in a clique in the generalized Paley graph whose edges join distinct elements differing by a nonzero cube. Thus the stated maximality assertion for the largest eligible subfield is false, including in the explicit simple-graph formulation.
lean_vs_paper: Lean checks the field and clique witness, largest eligible exponent and both maximality formulations. The paper separately proves that the 25-element span is a clique and that the prime field is maximal among subfield cliques. It gives a supplementary irreducibility argument and compares the result with the sufficient size condition.

title: The minimal surjective-strategy conjecture for wreath products
record_statement: Let $G\wr H$ be a wreath product with state group $K$, and call a surjective strategy **minimal** when it has the form $\{k_i\in K\}_{i=1}^{|K|-1}$. **Minimal strategy conjecture.** Whenever $G\wr H$ has a surjective strategy, it also has a minimal surjective strategy $\{k_i\in K\}_{i=1}^{|K|-1}$. Minimal strategies would give the shortest possible guaranteed bound discussed in the source; the conjecture is based on the examples known to the authors and remains open.
source: Peter Kagey, “Spinning switches on a wreath product”, arXiv:2210.09408 (2022).
row_statement: For a generalized spinning-switches puzzle with switch group G, a finite set of positions on which the adversary's group H acts, and state group K = G^Ω: if a strategy (a fixed sequence of moves that reaches every state whatever the adversary does) exists, then one of the minimal possible length |K| - 1 exists. This is Conjecture 41 of Kagey. The proof classifies when a strategy exists at all: only when |K| = 1, when H acts trivially, or when G and the image of H are p-groups for the same prime p. The new part is the obstruction: an invariant on cosets of p-subgroups shows that a switch group that is not a p-group can never win, in cases the source's quotient argument does not reach (for example A_5). For p-groups a minimal strategy is built by induction through a central subgroup of order p fixed by H. Lean defines the puzzle through the actual semidirect product, includes the initial state, and proves by computation that a strategy exists in a small nontrivial case and does not exist for S_3.

title: Conjecture on the partition-function bound in Harada's conjecture
record_statement:
For a positive integer $n$, let $p(n)$ be the number of partitions of $n$, and let $\Psi(\lambda)$ be the partition statistic used in the paper. Then

**Partition-function bound conjecture.** For $n\geq 7$,

$$
p(n)\binom{n}{2}-\sum_{\lambda\vdash n}\Psi(\lambda)>0.
$$

This inequality arises from the contribution of degree-one polynomials to the valuation polynomial associated with $h(\operatorname{GL}_n(k))$. Its validity would support the expected positivity behind the integrality of the Harada invariant in higher rank, but the conjecture is left open in the supplied text.
source: Masahiro Sugimoto, “Harada's conjecture II for the finite general linear groups and unitary groups”, arXiv:2304.10708 (2024).
row_statement: For every integer n ≥ 7, binom(n,2)p(n) − Σ_{λ⊢n} Ψ(λ) is strictly positive, where p(n) counts ordinary partitions and Ψ is binom(L,2)+Σᵢ(i−1)λᵢ+Σ_{j≥1} hⱼhⱼ₊₁ for positive row count L and column lengths hⱼ with zero tail.
lean_vs_paper: Lean checks both forms and their literal statistic. The group-valuation motivation in the paper supplies context. The endpoint is the standalone partition inequality.

title: The GM-rule Nash equilibrium conjecture for exact slow NIM
record_statement: Consider the exact slow game NIM$(n,n-1)$ for $\ell$ players: a position is a non-negative $n$-vector, players move cyclically, and on each move a player keeps one entry unchanged and decreases each of the other $n-1$ positive entries by $1$. A position with at least two non-positive entries is terminal; the player whose turn it is loses, and the other $\ell-1$ players share the payoff $\frac{C-L(P)}{\ell-1}$, where $L(P)$ is the play length and $C$ exceeds the length of every play from the initial position. The GM-rule specifies a strategy for each player, including the move that keeps the largest entry when no entry is a multiple of $\ell$. **GM-rule Nash equilibrium conjecture.** The set of $\ell$ GM-strategies forms a uniform Nash equilibrium. The claim concerns the strategic behavior induced by the GM-rule in the multiplayer exact slow NIM game; the supplied text does not state whether it has been proved or disproved.
source: Vladimir Gurvich and Mariya Naumova, “GM-rule and its applications to impartial games”, arXiv:2311.03257 (2023).
lean_endpoints: SlowNim360653.conjecture1_false : ¬ SlowNim360653.Conjecture, where Conjecture := for all n >= 2, l >= 2, initial positions x : Fin n -> N and rational C exceeding the length of every play from x under every legal positional profile, the all-GM profile (minimal multiple of l kept, largest index; largest entry kept when no multiple exists) is a Nash equilibrium for the payoff -(C - L) to the loser (player L mod l) and (C - L)/(l - 1) to each other player against every legal positional unilateral deviation; witnessed at n = l = 3, x = (4,4,5), C = 7
row_statement: In exact slow NIM with n ≥ 2 piles and ℓ ≥ 2 cyclic players, all-GM play can fail to be a Nash equilibrium against legal positional unilateral deviations, even with rational C above every legal play length. title: The integer-scaling criterion for C-realizability
record_statement:
Let $\{\frac{\lambda_1}{\alpha_1},\ldots,\frac{\lambda_n}{\alpha_n}\}$ be a multiset of rational numbers, and let $p=\operatorname{lcm}(\alpha_1,\ldots,\alpha_n)$. Here $C_{\mathbb{Q},3}$-realizability and $C_{\mathbb{Z},3}$-realizability refer to the corresponding realizability criteria for the Nonnegative Inverse Eigenvalue Problem.

**Integer-scaling criterion.** If $\{\frac{\lambda_1}{\alpha_1},\ldots,\frac{\lambda_n}{\alpha_n}\}$ is $C_{\mathbb{Q},3}$-realizable, then it is $C_{\mathbb{Q},3}$-realizable if and only if

$$
\left\{p\cdot\frac{\lambda_1}{\alpha_1},\ldots,p\cdot\frac{\lambda_n}{\alpha_n}\right\}
$$

is $C_{\mathbb{Z},3}$-realizable.

This criterion would remove the dependence on the particular sequence of realizability rules used to establish $C_{\mathbb{Q},3}$-realizability, reducing the question to an integer-scaled multiset whose scaling factor depends only on the denominators of the entries. The supplied text does not establish the equivalence, so its resolution is unclear.
source: Alberto Borobia and Roberto Canogar, “A simplification of the C-realizability criterion for the Nonnegative Inverse Eigenvalue Problem for integers”, arXiv:2401.07857 (2024).
row_statement: A rational multiset is C_{Q,3}-realizable exactly when its p-scaled integer multiset (p the least common multiple of the denominators) is C_{Z,3}-realizable; in fact every rational C3 derivation can be replaced by an integer one at scale p, and conversely. The C3 rules are those of the source's Theorem 7 and Definition 9: start from {0}, join two realizable multisets, raise the Perron root, or transfer a positive amount from the Perron root's partner to a nonpositive entry. The proof normalizes a derivation so that a leader absorbs finished blocks one at a time while an outstanding debt is passed up, and then shows that every step can be chosen as an integer in a closed-form region (the leaders are fixed by their terminal values and losing leaders are frozen), which is the integer-rounding statement no prior paper gives. Lean defines C3 inductively over an ordered ring, proves the unconditional direction rational-to-integer and its converse, and checks that C3 over ℤ holds for {1, −1} and fails for {−1}.

title: The square power partition function inequality conjecture
record_statement:
Let $p^k(n)$ denote the number of partitions of $n$ into perfect $k$-th powers. In particular, $p^2(n)$ is the square power partition function, and let $a,b$ be positive integers.

**Square power partition function inequality conjecture.** The inequality

$$
p^2(a)p^2(b)\geq p^2(a+b)
$$

has equality and failure exactly in the instances listed in the source's table: equality for $a=1$, $b=1,2,4,5,6,9,10,13,14,18,22$; $a=2$, $b=4,5,9,13$; $a=3$, $b=4$; $a=4$, $b=5,6,7$; $a=5$, $b=5,6,8,11,15$; $a=6$, $b=8,10,12,14$; and $a=7$, $b=8,9,12,13,19$, with the listed complementary instances of failure.

The claim refines the eventual multiplicative inequality for restricted partition functions by identifying its exceptional small-index behavior. The source gives no resolution beyond presenting these instances as a conjectural pattern.
source: Arindam Roy, “Log-concavity And The Multiplicative Properties of Restricted Partition Functions”, arXiv:2404.03153 (2025).
row_statement: For all positive integers a,b, put m=min(a,b), n=max(a,b), and let P count partitions into positive squares with unrestricted multiplicity, so that P(a)P(b)=P(a+b) exactly for n in the corresponding set in the list (1 → {1,2,4,5,6,9,10,13,14,18,22}, 2 → {4,5,9,13}, 3 → {4}, 4 → {5,6,7}, 5 → {5,6,8,11,15}, 6 → {8,10,12,14}, 7 → {8,9,12,13,19}). The product is smaller exactly at the remaining pairs with m=1,2,3 and at (5,7), (6,6), (6,7), (6,11), (6,15), (7,7), (7,10), (7,11), (7,14), (7,15), and it is strictly larger everywhere else.

title: The many-rank matrix-sum equidistribution conjecture
record_statement:
Let $\operatorname{Mat}^{n\times n}_q$ be the additive group of $n\times n$ matrices over $\mathbb F_q$. For integers $r_1,\ldots,r_k,t$ with $0\le r_i,t\le n$, let $\mathcal N^{n\times n}_q(r_1,\ldots,r_k;t)$ denote the number of $k$-tuples of matrices of respective ranks $r_1,\ldots,r_k$ whose sum is a fixed matrix of rank $t$, and let $\mathcal R^{n\times n}_q(r)$ denote the number of matrices of rank $r$. **Many-rank matrix-sum equidistribution conjecture.** For every $\epsilon>0$ there exists $K(\epsilon)$ such that, if $k\ge K(\epsilon)$ and $\epsilon n\le r_1,\ldots,r_k\le n$, then

$$
\mathcal N^{n\times n}_q(r_1,\ldots,r_k;t)=\operatorname{O}(1)\,\frac{\mathcal R^{n\times n}_q(r_1)\cdots\mathcal R^{n\times n}_q(r_k)}{q^{n^2}}.
$$

The source introduces this as the second of two conjectural generalizations of results in the paper; no resolution status is supplied.
source: Nick Gill, Noam Lifshitz, László Pyber and Endre Szabó, “Initiating the proof of the Liebeck–Nikolov–Shalev conjecture”, arXiv:2408.07800 (2024).
row_statement: For n x n matrices over F_q, if ranks r_1..r_k satisfy r_1+...+r_k >= 2n, then for every target T the number of k-tuples of matrices of those ranks summing to T is at most 32768 q^{-n^2} prod R(r_i). Hence Conjecture 5.5 of Gill-Lifshitz-Pyber-Szabo holds in its (source-intended) upper-bound reading, with K(eps)=ceil(2/eps) and an absolute constant.

title: Maximum sigma_t-irregularity conjecture for connected triangle-free graphs
record_statement:
Let $G$ be a connected triangle-free graph on $n$ vertices. Write $sigma_t(G)$ for its $sigma_t$-irregularity. Among such graphs, the extremal complete bipartite graphs are conjectured to have maximum $sigma_t(G)$.

**Triangle-free extremal conjecture.** Among connected triangle-free graphs on $n$ vertices, the extremal complete bipartite graphs have the maximum $sigma_t(G)$-irregularity.

then $P$ decomposes as a Cayley sum of lattice polytopes of dimension at most

$$
\left\lfloor 2(n+1-\mu(P)) \right\rfloor.
$$

The stronger conjecture by Dickenstein and Nill was disproved by Higashitani; the weaker version recorded here remains open. A slightly weaker statement, with the hypothesis $\mu(P) \geq \frac{n+2}{2}$, is known.
source: Sofía Garzón Mora and Christian Haase, “Fine Polyhedral Adjunction Theory”, arXiv:2302.04074 (2023).

title: The bunkbed conjecture for transitive tournaments
record_statement:
Let $T_n$ be the transitive tournament on $n$ vertices, and let $\operatorname{BBC}(E_7,T_n)$ denote the bunkbed conjecture in the $E_7$ model for $T_n$.

**The bunkbed conjecture for transitive tournaments.** The statement

$$
\operatorname{BBC}(E_7,T_n)
$$

holds for $T_n$.

The conjecture concerns whether the bunkbed inequality remains valid in the $E_7$ directed-graph model for this acyclic family. The supplied text does not state whether it has been resolved.
source: Lawrence Hollom, “The bunkbed conjecture is not robust to generalisation”, arXiv:2406.01790 (2024).
